series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-court-of-common-pleas.yml
series.subject_label: Allen County Court of Common Pleas
series.parameter: named holders of the common pleas bench serving Allen County, 1831–1920

points.label: The Allen County common pleas bench, 1833–1920
points.method: Transcribed by hand from the full text of both histories on archive.org. The count of 34 is the ten associate judges the 1921 book names between 1831 and 1851, the twenty presidents and judges the 1906 book names in sequence, and the four the 1921 book adds after 1906; Metcalf is counted once although the 1906 book gives him two spans. The three associate judges of 1831 are counted in the ten, not twice. It is a count of persons named as sitting, not of terms, and it is not a count of Allen County's own judges: for most of this period the seat was a multi-county one and the books name the holder's home county where they know it. Dates are given as printed, including the scan's "1S80" for James H. Day's start, which is reported here as 1880 and flagged nowhere else because the surrounding sentence dates his resignation to 1892. [verified]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: General Fund revenue

points.label: Allen County's General Fund, 2025
points.method: One PDF, the YTD summary revenue report for period 2025 12, and one more for expenditure, both converted with `pdftotext -layout` and parsed on the source's own `TOTAL` lines. The `as_of` is the date the report was generated, not the 31 December it is headed with, because the report was produced the day before the period it covers ended and the figures were still moving. Nothing is audited. Department figures are taken from the top of the source's own hierarchy: the sheriff's two sub-lines sum exactly to the office total, so adding every `TOTAL` line would double-count. [verified]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: audit reports released on Allen County public bodies

points.label: Every audit released on an Allen County public body, 1999–2026
points.method: One POST to the Auditor of State's audit search with `ddlCounty=Allen` and every other filter at its "all" option, returning all 1,260 rows unpaginated. [verified] Distinct bodies are counted after normalisation: a trailing report type in quotation marks is stripped from the entity name, `Inc.`, `LLC` and `dba` are dropped, and punctuation and case are ignored. That takes 1,260 strings to 141 spellings and 118 bodies; the raw distinct count is 174 and is not used. [verified] Years are release years, not audited periods, and the two can be eight years apart. [verified]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: ballots cast, general election

points.label: Allen County turnout, 2020 general election
points.method: Sum of the `ballots_cast` field over the 88 Allen County precincts, from a volunteer transcription of the certified returns. Registered voters summed the same way: 67,374. [verified]

points.label: Allen County turnout, 2004–2024
points.method: `F1a` against `A1a` for `FIPSCode` 3900300000 in each survey year, taking the 2004–2022 figures from the harmonised retrospective panel and 2024 from the separate 2024 release. [verified] `A1a` is the whole roll, active and inactive together; the active and inactive columns are not reported consistently across the eleven years and are not used. State figures are this corpus's own sums over all 88 Ohio county boards in the same files. Ballots by method sum exactly to the reported total in every year but 2024, where they fall 37 short. The mode table omits 2004 and 2006 because the survey did not separate early in-person voting from mail until 2010.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: boards of education of school districts holding ground in Allen County

points.label: The school boards of Allen County's twelve districts, 2026
points.method: Fetched from the Ohio boards of elections lookup by posting the district-type form with `cmbDistrictCat` = 8, which returns every school board in a county in one response — the same database the corpus previously read as eighty-eight separate precinct pages. Seats are the roster's own `Total Seats`. Names are printed as the Allen County view renders them, which is not always as a neighbouring county renders the same person; where they differ both are given and neither is corrected. Treasurers are excluded: they are appointed officers and not elective seats. [inference]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: election-day polling places

points.label: Allen County polling places and poll workers, 2004–2024
points.method: `D1a` precincts, `D3a` election-day polling places, `D4a` early-voting polling places and `D7a` poll workers with the `D7b`–`D7g` age bands, for `FIPSCode` 3900300000, taken from the harmonised retrospective panel for 2004–2022 and the separate 2024 release for 2024. [verified] `D3a` does not exist before 2008; the 2004 and 2006 rows show `D2a`, a combined polling-place count, which equals `D3a` in 2008, 2022 and 2024 and exceeds it by one in 2010 through 2016, so those two years are within one of the election-day count and not on the same footing as it. Ohio figures are this corpus's own sums over all 88 county boards. The state age comparison uses only the 73 counties whose age bands sum to their own reported total and who reported more than 50 workers.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: eviction cases filed

points.label: Eviction filings in Allen County, 2002–2018
points.method: The Eviction Lab's court-issued county file, `fips_county` 39003, seventeen years from 2002 to 2018. [verified] Rates are `filings_observed` over `renting_hh`, both from that file; the denominator is interpolated between census and survey vintages and moves smoothly every year. State figures are sums over all Ohio rows in the same file — 87 counties in every year but 2017, which has 88 — and the rank is of county filing rates within each year. The trend is an ordinary least-squares fit of the annual rate on the year with the standard error from the residuals; no correction is made for serial correlation, which would widen it. The legacy and proprietary series are held and not used here, and their spread against this one is recorded in the catalogue entry.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: four-year adjusted cohort graduation rate

points.label: Graduation rates in Allen County's twelve school districts, 2010–2019
points.method: One request per year, 2010 to 2019, to the EDFacts graduation-rate endpoint for Ohio, filtered here to the twelve districts by NCES identifier and to the all-students rows — the six subgroup dimensions all reading 99. [verified] County bounds weight each district's published lower and upper bound by its own `cohort_num`; an exact rate enters both sums at the same value. The midpoint column is not used anywhere on this page. State bounds are the same computation over every Ohio district with a positive cohort, 731 to 765 of them a year. `value` is Lima's 2019 rate, which is the only 2019 figure in the county published as a number.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: municipal corporations in Allen County with a recorded founding date

points.label: When Allen County's municipalities were incorporated, 1842–1904
points.method: Read from the full text of three county histories on archive.org, the 1885 book in two independent scans, and checked against the county's own cities-and-villages page. `as_of` is the latest founding date the corpus can state and not the query date, because the count is of corporations founded by then. Where two dates exist the table prints both and the `erected` property on each corporation carries the authorising one. Dates given only as a year are printed as a year; nothing here is promoted to a day. [inference]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: pupils proficient in reading, all grades

points.label: Reading and mathematics proficiency in Allen County's schools, 2009–2020
points.method: One request per year to the EDFacts assessment endpoint for Ohio at `grade-99`, 2009 to 2018 and 2020, filtered here to the twelve districts by NCES identifier and to the all-students rows. [verified] District figures are as published; through 2018 every one has `low` equal to `high`, and in 2020 the two band columns are null with the figure beside them populated, which is the same thing said a second way. [verified] County and state figures are computed here, weighting each district by its own count of valid tests — 9,308 for the county in 2018, 8,844 in 2020, and 905,315 and 835,596 for the state — and rows carrying the negative missing codes are excluded rather than read as zero. Gaps against the state are differences of the unrounded weighted figures, so 68.8 against 64.4 is stated as 4.4 and not 4.5. `value` is the county's own weighted reading figure for 2020, which is a derived number and not one the source prints.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: registrations removed from the voter roll

points.label: Removals from the Allen County voter roll, 2006–2022
points.method: `A9a` for `FIPSCode` 3900300000 summed over the nine survey years 2006 to 2022, from the harmonised retrospective panel. [verified] The 2024 survey reports every removal field as unavailable for this county, so the run stops at 2022. Each year's figure covers the period since the close of registration for the previous general election, so the nine years tile the whole of 2004–2022 without overlap. The reason table starts at 2008 because 2006 reports a total with almost no breakdown; within 2008–2022 the reasons fall 67 short of the totals. Shares are computed here against the 2008–2022 total of 55,243.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: seated holders of elective office, and seats vacant, by class of government

points.label: Allen County elective seats and how their holders arrived, 2026
points.method: Union of the eighty-eight precinct pages of the boards of elections roster, deduplicated on the office name and the page's own `hid_office` code. Vacancies are counted from its `N Vacant Seat(s)` rows and appointments from its `*Appointed*` marker; the class column is this corpus's grouping and the roster totals nothing. [verified] **It is a county's roster, so a ward seat of a city that crosses the county line does not appear.** Delphos contributes ten seats here and 3,182 of its people live in Van Wert County, so its council is undercounted by an unknown number of ward seats. [inference] No other government here is affected: Bluffton also crosses a line and elects its council at large.

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: total net position, primary government

points.label: Allen County's audited net position, 2023

Every figure is quoted from the report's own Table 1 and its Capital Assets and Debt Administration section, in the dollars it prints and without rounding. The changes between 2022 and 2023 are subtractions of two printed figures and are marked as computed. The report labels its management discussion "Unaudited"; the statements it discusses are audited, and the figures above are from the statements. [verified]

series.subject: jurisdiction/allen-county-government.yml
series.parameter: total revenue recorded across all county funds

points.label: What passes through Allen County's books, 2025

The per-fund figures sum to the grand totals the reports themselves print, which is the check that the parse is complete: 437 funds to $374,841,546.99 and 413 to $370,746,613.34. Custodial funds are identified by their fund number beginning 9 and by the equality of their two sides, not by any label the source applies, because the source applies none. [verified]

series.parameter: voting districts

points.label: Allen County voting districts, 2020

series.parameter: seated holders of the city's elective offices

points.label: The elective government of Lima, 2026

series.subject: jurisdiction/lima-city-school-district.yml

series.subject: jurisdiction/lima-city-school-district.yml

series.subject: jurisdiction/village-of-bluffton.yml
series.parameter: municipal elections in Allen County villages reported with returns

points.label: Municipal elections in Bluffton and Beaverdam as their paper reported them, 1939–1959
points.method: The election-week issue of each odd year from 1939 to 1959 that the archive holds, read page by page from the ALTO OCR: 1939, 1943, 1945, 1947, 1955, 1957 and 1959. 1941, 1949, 1951 and 1953 have no issue in the week after the election and are absent for that reason and not because nothing was printed. Six of the seven read carry a Bluffton mayoral result and two carry Beaverdam's, which is the eight counted below; 1947 carries the campaign and not the count. series.subject: natural-feature/great-black-swamp.yml
series.parameter: original vegetation cover by type
series.unit: acres of elm-ash swamp forest, of 260,358.7

points.label: What grew in Allen County before the surveys, mapped
points.method: The statewide shapefile filtered by a spatial filter on the county polygon, each polygon intersected with it, and the intersections projected to EPSG:6549 for area. [verified] The thirteen vegetation names come from the enumerated domain in the file's own FGDC metadata and not from any re-hosted copy with the names already joined. [verified] Township shares divide the swamp area inside each 2024 county subdivision by that subdivision's own projected area, so Lima is listed as the separate unit the boundary file makes it. [verified] The hydric figures are the corpus's own, from the soil survey, and the two sources compute county area 18.7 acres apart — 260,340 against 260,358.7 — which is 0.007 per cent and is not reconciled here. [verified]

series.subject: natural-feature/ottawa-river.yml
series.parameter: bridges crossing the Ottawa River in Allen County

points.label: What Allen County's bridges cross, 2025
points.method: Counted here from the 2025 Ohio file, selecting Allen County and matching `FEATURES_DESC_006A` and `FACILITY_CARRIED_007` by substring. Those fields are free text entered by the state and are inconsistently abbreviated, so a bridge described as "AUGLAIZE RIVER FAULKNER" is counted to the Auglaize and one described as "STREAM SLABTOWN RD" is counted to nothing. The counts are therefore floors, and the residue is structures over unnamed water. [inference]

series.subject: natural-feature/ottawa-river.yml
series.parameter: highest recorded peak flow on the Ottawa River

points.label: Peak flows on the Ottawa River, 1924–2025
points.method: Fetched from the USGS peak-streamflow service for site 04187500 and 04187100 and counted here by water year, which runs 1 October to 30 September and is named for the year it ends in. The two gauges are not combined into one series and no figure here is computed across both. The `value` is the largest peak either gauge recorded and the `as_of` is the day it happened, which is not the same as the largest flow the river has ever carried: the record covers 79 of the 102 years between 1924 and 2025, and none before. [inference]

series.subject: natural-feature/scioto-river-basin.yml
series.parameter: elevation of the land surface, and the length of the continental divide within it

points.label: How high Allen County is, 2026
points.method: The elevation surface was exported over a bounding box of the county at 1,600 × 880 cells and clipped to [TIGER's 2024 county polygon](../../catalog/census-tiger-roads.md) with a cutline. [verified] The image service returns metres and the point service returns whatever it is asked for; every figure here is stated in feet and the conversion is 3.280839895. [verified] Natural relief excludes one contiguous component: the cells reachable from the county minimum without rising above 800 feet, which is 188 cells and 47.7 acres. The rim used for the pit's depth is the median of the 78 cells that touch that component from outside, not an annulus, so it is the ground the pit was cut into. [verified] The divide is `WBDLine` features carrying `hudigit` 2 — the boundary between two-digit hydrologic regions — intersected with the county polygon and measured in EPSG:6549, Ohio North in US survey feet; the projection was checked first by projecting the county polygon and comparing its area to the published one, agreeing to 0.010 per cent. [verified] Samples along the divide are every 500 feet of its projected length.

series.subject: office/allen-county-board-of-commissioners.yml
series.parameter: men named as county commissioner, 1831–1920

points.label: The Allen County board of commissioners, 1831–1920
points.method: The 1906 list was parsed from the archive.org full text and then checked by hand against the scan, because the OCR breaks names across lines and the shift-register test is worthless if a name is wrong in one row and right in the next: "H. B. Thorn" for Henry B. Thorn in 1837 alone would have manufactured two departures. Four such artifacts were reconciled — that abbreviation, "Bernard Escli" for Esch, "Franeis M. Clum" for Francis, and a stray comma in "Alexander, Conrad" — and each is a scan defect rather than a difference between editions. The 1921 list was transcribed by hand. The count of 68 is persons: fifty-three in the dated list plus fifteen names the 1921 book adds after Charles W. Johnston, with the initialled forms matched to their full forms only where the surname and the position in sequence both agree. [verified]

series.subject: office/allen-county-sheriff.yml
series.parameter: violent offenses reported by the Allen County Sheriff's Office

points.label: Offenses reported by the Allen County Sheriff, 2015–2024
points.method: Monthly counts summed to calendar years. The two periods are divided at the office's own incident-based reporting start of 1 December 2020, so 2020 sits in the earlier period and 2021 in the later; the one month of overlap is not adjusted for. No figure here is computed across the two periods except the ratio, which is reported precisely to show that the two measures move opposite ways. [inference]

series.subject: office/mayor-of-lima.yml
series.parameter: entries in the printed lists of Lima's mayors beginning after April 1886

points.label: The mayors of Lima, 1886–1922
points.method: Read from the 1906 history's dated list of mayors and the 1921 history's undated ordered list, which are very likely one lineage rather than two witnesses: the 1921 book says it is following "the most recent report in Lima", which "enumerates the mayors from the beginning". Dates to 1904 are the 1906 book's. Dates after 1904 are computed here from that book's last dated entry, the 1921 book's statement of the two-year term, and the 1 January 1922 abolition, and are reported as an inference that closes rather than as a source's dating. The count is of entries as printed. It is not a count of terms and not a count of men: the lists give a consecutive re-election its own entry twice and fold three terms into one entry once. [inference]

series.subject: office/mayor-of-lima.yml
series.parameter: mayors of Lima, 1842 to 1886

points.label: The mayors of Lima, 1842-1886
points.method: Read from the 1885 county history's chapter on Ottawa Township and Lima City, which narrates the municipal elections year by year from 1842 to 1873 and then prints a list of mayors from 1873 to 1885. Both archive.org digitizations were read and compared line by line; they agree on every name and differ only where scan A substitutes a digit or a letter, each of which is resolved by the sequence rather than by preferring a scan. [verified] Terms are counted as continuous runs under one man, so a re-election is not a new term and the three men who returned after an interval are counted twice. Years are the years of election as the book gives them; the book runs by election year and not by term, so a range like 1851-53 is "elected in 1851, succeeded by the man elected in 1853" and not an assertion about the day either man took office. [inference]

series.subject: office/mayor-of-lima.yml
series.parameter: mayors of Lima named in a contemporaneous source, 1939–1956

points.label: Mayors of Lima named inside the gap, 1939–1956
points.method: Four full-text searches of one newspaper title, and the ALTO OCR of every hit page read in full. "Mayor of Lima" and "Lima mayor" return 22 hits across 21 issues and supply ten of the rows above; "Mayor McClain" supplies two, "Metheany" one, and one more came out of an election-week issue read for another purpose. Nothing here is a term: each row is the date the paper printed the words, not a date the person took or left office, and no row is used to date another. Corbin Shook is counted among the five as a former mayor and is not placed in time. [verified]

series.subject: organization/mercy-health-st-ritas-medical-center.yml
series.parameter: inpatient discharges, patient days and the outpatient share of charges

points.label: What Allen County's hospitals did, 2011–2023
points.method: One row per hospital per fiscal year for CCNs 360009, 360066, 360263, 361322 and 362020, from the thirteen final cost report files FY2011 through FY2023; where a hospital filed twice in a year the first row is taken, as in [the bed node](allen-county-hospital-beds-2011-2023.yml). [verified] Discharges and days are the `V + XVIII + XIX + Unknown` totals, which is every payer and not Medicare alone. [verified] Average stay is patient days over discharges and occupancy is patient days over total bed days available, both computed on county totals rather than averaged across hospitals. [verified] The outpatient share is outpatient charges over the sum of inpatient and outpatient charges in the same year, which makes it a ratio of two list-price columns and immune to the inflation in either. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County Republican presidential share less Ohio's, 1980–2008
series.unit: percentage points, mean of eight elections

points.label: Allen County's Republican share against Ohio's and the nation's, 1980–2008
points.method: The differences use the file's own percentages, which are printed to one decimal for every area, so each difference is good to about two tenths of a point and the 2.7-point band is wider than that error by an order of magnitude. Ranks and the all-eight counts were computed from the vote counts instead, because rounded percentages tie counties that are not tied. Eight elections is what the file holds; it begins at 1980 and stops at 2008, and the corpus's [1960 and 1964](allen-county-presidential-vote-1960-1964.yml) come from a volume that prints only the leading party's share and so cannot extend this table. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County housing units

points.label: Allen County's housing in 1990
points.method: CH-1-37 and CH-2-37, Table 1, county summary rows, read from `pdftotext -layout` output. [verified] The volumes print shares against a base they also print, so counts recovered from a share carry the rounding of one decimal place — about twenty-one units on a base of forty-two thousand — and every such conversion here says "about". [inference] The 1990 owner-occupancy and room figures are from the complete count; plumbing, kitchen, telephone, vehicles and year built are from the sample and carry sampling error the volume does not print. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men in United States service, Civil War

points.label: Allen County in United States service, 1861-1865
points.method: Read from the military chapter of the 1885 county history, whose roster covers 1861-1865 and was compiled twenty years after the close. The 1,920 is the compiler's own total of his own list, stated twice. The check is a parse of the roster text from both archive.org digitizations of the book: entries are detected as a capitalised surname following a sentence break and followed by a given name, filtered against a stop list of place names, months, unit words and running heads, and validated against the alphabetical order the roster is printed in. Scan B yields 1,877 records and scan A 1,745, against 1,920 printed. [inference] The regiment ranking is computed from the same records and is reported as a ranking rather than as counts, because the two scans disagree on the counts by up to a factor of two — scan A renders "81st" variously as "8l8t" and "Slst" — and agree on the order of the first six. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men in military or naval service, First World War

points.label: Allen County in the World War — how many served
points.method: Every line of Elmer McClain's printed roster matching `Surname, Given` or `Surname. Given`, counted from the single archive.org digitization of the 1921 history — 4,088 plus 70. Ninety-six further lines were rejected and are reported rather than estimated. Duplicates were not removed from the published figure; they are counted separately. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men recorded as dying in United States service, Civil War

points.label: Allen County's Civil War dead, counted from the roster
points.method: Both archive.org digitizations of the 1885 county history were parsed into roster records — a capitalised surname after a sentence break, followed by a given name — over the five sections of Chapter IX's roster, filtered against a stop list of place names, months, unit words and running heads. Scan B yields 1,877 records and scan A 1,745, against a printed 1,920. A record counts as a death if it carries any of: `died`, an abbreviated `d.` followed by a date or a place, `killed`, `k'd`, `k'l'd`, `k.` before a place, `mortally`, `drowned`, or `lost on`. The published value is the **lower** of the two scans, because every failure mode here — an unrecognised entry, an OCR-mangled abbreviation, a roster silent about a man's fate — pushes the count down, and none pushes it up. [inference] Place of death is counted only where the place name falls within one clause of the word recording the death, so that a man who enlisted at one place and died at another is not counted twice. The two scans agree exactly at Corinth and Atlanta and differ by one at Nashville. Regiment counts are **not** published: the two scans differ on those by up to a factor of two, because one of them reads "81st" as "8l8t". [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County men who died in service, First World War

points.label: Allen County's World War dead
points.method: Every line of the printed honour roll matching `Surname, Given`, counted from the single digitization of the 1921 history. Two rejected lines were identified as wrapped continuations of accepted names and are not additional men. Overlap with the service roster computed on normalised surname plus first initial. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Allen County vacant housing units classed other vacant

points.label: Why Allen County's housing was empty, 2019–2023
points.method: Table-based summary file, 2019–2023 five-year estimates, table B25004, whose universe is vacant housing units. [verified] The 2020 column is table H5 of [the census characteristics file](../../catalog/census-2020-dhc.md) as already published on [the census node](allen-county-vacancy-status-2010-2020.yml), reprinted here for the comparison and not recomputed. [verified] County ranks are over all 88 Ohio and 3,203 national county records in the survey file; sixteen of the country's 3,219 counties are left out of the national rank because their vacant-unit base is under a hundred. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Army dead and missing credited to Allen County

points.label: Allen County's Army dead and missing, 1941–1946
points.method: Read from the page images of the Ohio volume: the tabulation page for the six category counts and the two county pages for the roll. The 171 and its six components are the tabulation's own figures, transcribed and checked to sum. The count of names was made from the same images — 69 in the first column, 70 in the second, 32 on the following page — and is reported as a check on the printed total rather than as a substitute for it. No name is transcribed here: this corpus counts war rolls and does not copy them, as it did for [1861](allen-county-civil-war-service.yml) and [1917](allen-county-world-war-service.yml). [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Atmospheric Crude Distillation Capacity (barrels per calendar day), Total Operable

points.label: Lima refinery operator and crude capacity, 1994–2026

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Black residents of Allen County, as estimated

points.label: Allen County's Black community, 1916–1921
points.method: Read from the full text of the 1921 county history on archive.org. Every figure is the book's estimate and the book says so — "it is estimated", "almost", "about" — and none is a count. The quotations are transcribed as printed, including the period's terminology, because paraphrase would silently improve a source this corpus is also reporting the limits of. The 1920 population against which the share is computed is the census figure the corpus already holds, not the book's. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Black share of enrolment in the county's twelve school districts

points.label: Who the children in Allen County's schools are, 1988–2024
points.method: One request per year to the district enrolment endpoint for Ohio, `grade-99`, all race codes, filtered here to the twelve districts by NCES identifier. Race codes are 1 white, 2 Black, 3 Hispanic, 4 Asian, 5 American Indian or Alaska Native, 6 Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, 7 two or more, 9 unknown and 99 total; codes 4 to 6 and 9 are held and not printed above, and the county's Asian enrolment is 185 in 1988 and 121 now. Every share is computed here from counts. [verified] Category 7 is absent before 2010 and is shown as an em dash rather than a zero for that reason; see [a zero is not a blank](../../decisions/a-zero-is-not-a-blank.yml).

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: COVID-19 cases and hospitalisations of county residents

points.label: COVID-19 cases and hospitalisations in Allen County, 2020–2023
points.method: Cases are dated to onset and hospitalisations to admission, and both are counted on the row where they appear rather than on the row's other dates. [verified] Rates per hundred thousand use the 2020 census counts of 102,206 and 11,799,448; the ranking across the eighty-eight counties uses CDC's own population column for all of them, so that no county is advantaged by its denominator. [verified] The 292 admissions without a date are included in every county total here and excluded from every yearly one, and the yearly columns therefore sum to 1,944 rather than to 2,236. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: COVID-19 deaths by county of death against county of residence
series.unit: deaths in the county, against 513 of its residents

points.label: Where Allen County's COVID-19 deaths happened, 2020–2023
points.method: The two figures come from two files captured on the same day, ninety-eight seconds apart, and not from the residence file's own later capture: a residence count from September against a death count from May would put four months of revision into a ratio. [verified] County names are stripped before grouping, because the residence file names each county twice and the padded block is the deaths that occurred outside Ohio — 1,336 rows and 1,344 deaths, concentrated in the border counties, and two of them Allen County's. A reader who groups on the raw string reports Gallia's ratio as 1.92 rather than 1.54. [verified] The ranking is restricted to the eighty-two counties with a hundred or more resident deaths, because a ratio on a denominator of thirty is not a comparable quantity. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: COVID-19 deaths of county residents

points.label: COVID-19 deaths of Allen County residents, 2020–2023
points.method: Rows are selected on the county name after stripping, because the file names Allen County twice — once plainly and once padded to a fixed width — and the padded block is the deaths that occurred outside Ohio. Two of this county's 517 are in it. [verified] Deaths are dated to the date of death, cases to the date of onset and hospitalisations to the date of admission, so the three counts on one row are independent and no row contributes to more than one of them. [verified] The rate per hundred thousand divides by the 2020 census counts — 102,206 for the county and 11,799,448 for the state — and the ranking across Ohio's counties uses one consistent denominator instead, CDC's county population column, for all eighty-eight. [verified] The last weeks of the record are provisional in the ordinary way of a death file and are not adjusted here. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: FTE - Employees on Payroll

points.label: Allen County hospital employment, 2011–2023
points.method: CCNs 360009, 360066, 360263, 361322 and 362020 across the thirteen annual files — 66 rows. County totals sum the four calendar-year filers; [Kindred](../organization/kindred-hospital-lima.yml) left the calendar year after FY2013, so FY2014 holds two of its rows. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Number of Beds

points.label: Allen County hospital beds, 2011–2023
points.method: `Number of Beds` for CCNs 360009, 360066, 360263, 361322 and 362020. The total takes one row per hospital per year, which in FY2014 means Kindred's first row only — it filed twice that year across a change of fiscal year. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Republican share of all votes cast for U.S. Representative

points.label: Allen County's vote for Congress, 2000–2020
points.method: County-grain files where they exist; 2006, 2010 and 2018 summed over the county's precincts. 2004 has no Ohio general-election file in the repository at any grain, so it is absent rather than zero. Shares are of every vote recorded in the race, including minor candidates, rather than of the two-party vote. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: Republican share of the two-party vote for governor

points.label: Allen County vote for governor, 2002–2018
points.method: 2002, 2014 and 2018 are county-grain files. 2006 and 2010 are summed over the county's 139 and 121 precincts respectively, from the Secretary of State's own workbooks; the 2010 file's `COUNTY TOTALS` row is excluded from the sum and used to check it. Vote counts in the 2006 and 2010 files are written as floating-point numbers and are converted here; every value is integral. [verified] Shares are of the two major-party candidates only, computed here. The 2010 file carries no party column and party for that year is this corpus's, from the candidates. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: USGS water monitoring sites in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's water monitoring sites, 2026
points.method: Fetched from the USGS site service with `siteStatus=all`, which is required or discontinued gauges are omitted — and the discontinued ones carry most of the county's long record. Site types are the service's own two-letter codes, collapsed here to their first letter group. The count is of sites the service lists for this county whatever their status or period of record, and is not a count of instruments now running. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas overlapping Allen County

points.label: Allen County's ZIP codes, 2020
points.method: `tab20_zcta520_tabblock20_natl.txt`, the 2020 ZCTA-to-block relationship file, streamed and filtered to the twenty tabulation areas that touch county 39003, joined on the fifteen-digit block identifier to block populations from the Ohio P.L. 94-171 file. A block's county is the first five characters of its identifier, so the county split needs no second lookup. [verified] Population shares are the sum of block populations in each county part over the area's total. Land shares are `AREALAND_PART` over the area's total land, which is what the county-level relationship file publishes and the only figure available without the block join. [verified] Post-office names are the modal `CITY` value on the contribution records carrying each code in the four cycles from 2012, not a postal directory. [verified] — [the contributions](allen-county-federal-contributions-1980-2024.yml). The relationship files carry no name for a ZCTA beyond its number. Blocks appearing more than once against the same area — the file lists a row per overlap — are counted once. The county parts sum to 102,206 against a published county population of 102,206. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: acres entering the developed land cover classes, Allen County

points.label: Allen County developed land and impervious surface, 2001–2021
points.method: Impervious surface is published as per-cent cover per pixel; the acreage here is the sum of those percentages over the county divided by a hundred, which is the only reading that makes the figure additive. Values above 100 are the product's own codes for roads outside the developed classes and are excluded, which affects nothing at this county's scale. The transition figures are counted between consecutive epochs rather than between the endpoints, because a pixel that changes twice is one acre of change in the endpoint comparison and two in the stepwise one, and the question here is how often the file permits a direction. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: annexations reported to the Boundary and Annexation Survey

points.label: Allen County annexations, 1990–2024
points.method: Every row of Ohio's BAS boundary-change files whose entity FIPS place code is one of the ten Allen County places — Beaverdam 04752, Bluffton 07426, Cairo 10884, Delphos 21602, Elida 24808, Fort Shawnee 27944, Harrod 34118, Lafayette 41118, Lima 43554, Spencerville 74034. Sixteen tab-delimited files, two record layouts, joined on the fields the readme names. Delphos and Bluffton cross county lines and the pre-2018 layout carries no county column, so their totals include ground on the Van Wert and Hancock sides. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: annual mean temperature, Allen County

points.label: Allen County temperature, 1895–2025
points.method: Six county files taken from the same NOAA release and parsed on the eleven-character key `33003`, where 33 is NOAA's alphabetical code for Ohio and not its FIPS code. Only complete calendar years are used, so 2026 is excluded and the record runs 1895 through 2025 without a gap. The strongest check available was run first and passed: the average, maximum and minimum temperature files are separate downloads, and across Allen County's 1,572 complete monthly cells `(tmax + tmin) / 2` equals the average file to within a rounding step, the largest disagreement in the whole record being 0.10 °F. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: annual precipitation, Allen County

points.label: Allen County precipitation, 1895–2025
points.method: Parsed on the eleven-character key `33003` from the same NOAA release as the temperature files, element code 01. Complete calendar years only: a year with any month coded −9.99 is dropped, so the record runs 1895 through 2025 with no gap and 2026 is excluded. Annual figures are the sum of the twelve printed monthly values and the thirty-year figures are the mean of those sums. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: applicants paid federal public assistance for work in Allen County

points.label: Who was paid federal disaster aid in Allen County, 2005–2025
points.method: Distinct `applicantId` across the county's 95 project rows, resolved to names through the applicant register with the filter scoped to Ohio. Scoping is required: `003-99003-00`, the identifier the county government itself files under, returns more than a hundred and eighty county governments across the United States and an unscoped join names a Delaware one. Dollars are the federal share obligated, nominal, summed per applicant and rounded to the dollar; the table's rounded rows do not sum exactly to the total published in [the assistance measure](allen-county-disaster-assistance-2005-2025.yml). Parenthesised county names are the file's own. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: audit reports carrying a finding for recovery

points.label: Findings for recovery against Allen County public bodies, 1999–2026
points.method: The asterisk prefix on the entity name in the result table, which the table's own footnote defines as "Denotes Findings for Recovery". [verified] The search form's `cbxFindingsForRecovery` checkbox returns no rows at all when sent and is not used. [verified] Bodies are counted after the same normalisation the audit roster uses. Rates are reports with a finding over reports of that class, not bodies over bodies, because a body audited annually has more chances to carry one than a body audited every second year. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: average daily population of the Allen County jail

points.label: Allen County's jail, 1970–2023
points.method: `incarceration_trends_county.csv` filtered on `county_fips = 39003`, 43 rows, against the state file for Ohio. Rates are the file's own, per 100,000 residents aged 15 to 64, and are not comparable with any rate this corpus computes over a whole population. [verified] The jail population is BJS's average daily population; capacity is the rated capacity reported with it. [verified] The 2000 row and the 2020 admissions figure are excluded by hand and the exclusion is stated rather than silent. [inference] Occupancy is population over rated capacity in the 29 years carrying both, 2000 excluded.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: average weekly wage, all industries, all ownerships

points.label: What work pays in Allen County, 2024
points.method: QCEW annual averages, aggregation level 74 for the sector table and 70 for the county total, read from the BLS open CSV API. Sector figures are summed across ownership codes, so a sector's row includes its government establishments; average annual pay per sector is total annual wages divided by average annual employment, which is this corpus's arithmetic over the source's two published fields. The eighteen sectors sum to 49,113 jobs against the county total of 49,690; the residual is employment the file places at aggregation levels this table does not read. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: ballots cast, general election

points.label: Allen County's ballot, 7 November 2006
points.method: Summed over the county's 139 precincts from `gen06statewide.csv`, the Secretary of State's own workbook, which has no county-total row; the volunteer transcription of the same election in the same repository agrees with it on every figure to the vote, and the two are one witness rather than two — the repository carries a parser named for converting one into the other. [inference] Vote counts are floating-point in that file and are converted here; every value is integral. Shares are of the two major-party candidates only, computed here.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: buildings in Allen County

points.label: The buildings of Allen County, 2019
points.method: All rows with `FIPS='39003'`, taken in thirty pages of 2,000 ordered by `OBJECTID`, without geometry; the file's own `LONGITUDE` and `LATITUDE` were projected from NAD83 to EPSG:26916 and written to a GeoPackage, and every containment test below is that centroid inside the polygon. [verified] A centroid rule assigns a building that straddles a line to one side of it, and 129 buildings in this county sit within ten metres of a subdivision boundary. [inference] Footprint areas are the file's `SQFEET`, summed. Subdivision and place polygons are the 2024 TIGER files clipped to the county, which is why Bluffton and Delphos are counted only for the part of them inside Allen County. [verified] Individual buildings were fetched with geometry one query at a time, and the ten site tests are point-in-polygon against the service rather than against a centroid. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: buildings inside the special flood hazard area, Allen County

points.label: Allen County's buildings inside the mapped floodplain, 2026
points.method: The hazard area is the union of every National Flood Hazard Layer polygon flagged `SFHA_TF='T'` for `DFIRM_ID='39003C'`, clipped to the 2024 TIGER county polygon, as computed for [the mapped floodplain](allen-county-flood-hazard-2026.yml). [verified] A building is inside if its centroid is; no footprint was intersected, so a large building on the edge of a zone counts once and on one side. [inference] Block weights are residential buildings only: for each 2020 block, the count inside the hazard area divided by the count in the block, applied to `POP20` and `HOUSING20`. Blocks with no residential building contribute nothing and are reported separately rather than distributed. [verified] Place shares are computed against each place clipped to this county, so Bluffton and Delphos are counted only for their Allen County parts, the same convention the flood-hazard node uses. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: cancer death rate, all sites, age-adjusted

points.label: What cancer does in Allen County, 2018–2023
points.method: The value above is the all-sites age-adjusted death rate for the five years 2019–2023, dated here by the last year of that window as this corpus dates its other multi-year mortality measures. State Cancer Profiles' CSV output — `output=1` — for Ohio counties, one request per site and per stratum, nineteen sites for mortality and four for incidence. A site code with no dataset behind it returns an HTML page under HTTP 200, so every response is checked against its first line before parsing; twenty-eight codes were tried and nineteen are real. Rates are the file's own age-adjusted figures and ranks are the file's own `CI*Rank`, not computed here. Mortality covers 2019–2023 and incidence 2018–2022, and no figure combines the two. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: certified nursing homes, beds and average residents per day

points.label: Allen County nursing homes, 2026
points.method: All 922 Ohio rows pulled from the Care Compare provider file; county membership settled by Census address ranges on each provider's street address rather than by the file's own county column, and cross-checked against point-in-polygon on the published coordinates. Deficiency counts are every row in the health-deficiency file for the twelve certification numbers. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: certified school librarians in the county's twelve districts

points.label: What Allen County's twelve school districts employ, 1992–2024
points.method: One request per year to the Common Core of Data district directory for Ohio, 1986 to 2024, filtered here to the same twelve NCES agency identifiers the enrolment series uses. Values of `-1` and `-2` are treated as missing and never summed; a year is marked complete only when all twelve districts report the column, and the pupils-per-teacher ratio is left blank in any year they do not. Staffing columns are empty before 1992 and the series therefore starts there, seven years after the enrolment it is read against. The `year` is the autumn the count was taken, so 2024 is the 2024–25 school year. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: channel distance from Allen County to the end of the network

points.label: How far Allen County's water is from the sea, 2026
points.method: `PathLength` on every NetworkNHDFlowline reach with length inside the 2024 TIGER county polygon, converted at 1.609344 km to the mile. The field measures from the downstream end of the reach, so the shortest figure belongs to the last reach of the Auglaize before it leaves the county and the longest to a headwater. [verified] The 858 metres is between the upstream endpoints of the two reaches in EPSG:26916 and is a straight line, not a walk. [verified] Terminal identity is read from `TerminalPa` and the terminating reach's own name, not from the most common name on its level path. [verified] — see [a level path is not a river](../../decisions/a-level-path-is-not-a-river.yml).

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: children in private schools, Allen County

points.label: Allen County's private and community schools, 2013–2021
points.method: Filtered on `PSTABB` = `OH` and `PCNTY` = `003`, which is state abbreviation and county FIPS rather than the five-digit code every other file here uses; the survey's own composite runs county-then-state and reads `00339`. Column names are not stable across editions — 2015–16 lower-cases every header — so each file's headers were upper-cased before matching, and a first pass that matched `NUMSTUDS` exactly silently found nothing for that year. Community schools are the 2022 Common Core of Data filtered on `county_code` = `39003` and `charter` = 1, after downloading all 3,695 Ohio rows: the API accepts a `county_code` parameter and ignores it. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: communicants in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's churches, 1906 and 1921
points.method: Read from the full text of the 1906 and 1921 county histories on archive.org. The 1921 figure is the book's own report of a survey it does not name a date for; the corpus dates it 1920 from the population it implies and marks that an inference. Bluffton's memberships are transcribed as the 1906 book prints them and are not summed into any county total, because no comparable count exists for the rest of the county in either book. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: counties erected from the cession by the act of 12 February 1820

points.label: The Ohio counties of 1820 and the names Howe gives them
points.method: Read from the whitespace-normalised full text of both Howe editions on archive.org, entry by entry rather than by search, because the formation sentence is the only place an attribution appears and a keyword search for "named in honor" returns two of the eleven. The 1847 edition gives "formed ... April 1st, 1820" for thirteen of the fourteen and gives Marion only an organization date of 1824; the fourteenth name is taken from [the 1921 county history](../../catalog/rusler-allen-county-1921.md), which lists the group the act provided for and includes Union, a county erected by a different act five weeks earlier. The discrepancy is reported rather than resolved. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: county population less the city of Lima, decennial

points.label: Allen County outside Lima, 1890–2020
points.method: Subtraction of the city count from the county count at each census, both from Census publications this corpus already holds and cites. Not a published figure: no source states it, and it is tagged as this corpus's inference throughout. The `value` above is the series maximum. Boundaries are as reported at each census and are known to have moved in 1902, 1903, 1905, 1906, 1944 and between 1980 and 1990 — twice out of the city and four times into it. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: crop acreage and production, Allen County

points.label: Allen County crops, 2022, against 1909
points.method: Census of Agriculture, harvested acreage and production for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file. The 1909 column is the Thirteenth Census, enumerated April 15 1910 for the 1909 crop year. Yields are computed here by dividing production by harvested acres, which is not how either census reports yield and is comparable only because both report both terms. [inference] `(D)` is a suppressed cell, not a zero; a dash is a crop the source does not name for this county in that year, which for 1909 soybeans is a statement about the volume's crop list and not a count of zero acres. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: cumulative COVID-19 cases per 100,000 by ZIP code

points.label: COVID-19 cases by ZIP code in and around Allen County, 2020–2023
points.method: Rates are the file's own, computed by Ohio on its own population column, and are reproduced rather than recomputed so that they remain comparable with each other. [verified] The county estimate weights each code's cumulative cases by the share of that code's 2020 census population living in Allen County, from the corpus's own ZCTA join, which sums to 102,206 — the county exactly. [verified] Only codes with a majority of their people in the county are tabulated above; the other nine of the twenty contribute to the weighted estimate and not to the ordering. [verified] The file's last-30-day and last-14-day columns read `N/A` throughout and are not used. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: days at unhealthy for sensitive groups or worse, as a share of days monitored

points.label: What the monitors measured over Allen County, 1980–2024
points.method: The EPA AirData annual AQI-by-county file for each year 1980–2024, unzipped, filtered to the row where `State` is Ohio and `County` is Allen. Shares are computed against `Days with AQI` rather than against 365. The six severity columns sum to `Days with AQI` in all forty-five rows and so do the per-pollutant columns, which is how the partition was confirmed. Ranks are over Ohio rows present in that year's file and are ranks among the monitored. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: deaths in crashes at highway-rail grade crossings

points.label: Deaths at Allen County railway crossings, 1980–2005
points.method: Crashes in the NHTSA accident file for Ohio county 3 whose `RAIL` value is neither `0000000` nor the `*******` fill of 1975–1978, joined to the FRA grade crossing inventory on `crossingid`. [verified] The join is case-insensitive because one record spells a crossing `532715r` and another `532715R`. The inventory is a current snapshot retrieved in 2026, so its closures and gate arms describe the crossings now and not at the date of any crash; `cityname` in it is the nearest named place and two of those, Cridersville and Columbus Grove, lie outside the county even though the crossings do not. The Poisson figure treats the 1980–2005 crashes as a constant-rate process, which is the null being rejected and not a description of the world.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: deaths in motor vehicle crashes

points.label: Deaths on Allen County roads, 1975–2024
points.method: NHTSA's national accident file for each year 1975 to 2024, filtered to `STATE` 39 and `COUNTY` 3, decoded as `utf-8-sig` because two of the fifty files carry a byte-order mark. [verified] Deaths are the sum of `FATALS`, which counts everyone who died within thirty days of the crash, including people not in a vehicle. Rates per 100,000 use the decennial census count nearest each decade's middle — 112,241 for 1975–1984, then 109,755, 108,464, 106,331 and 102,217 — so a decade's rate is a ten-year average against one population and not a mean of ten annual rates. The state and national figures are this corpus's own sums over every county row of the same files. The road-class table begins in 1987 because `ROUTE` does; the alcohol series ends in 2020 because `DRUNK_DR` leaves the file.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: domestic animals on and off farms, Allen County

points.label: Allen County domestic animals, on farms and off, 1910
points.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: on the farms the seven animal values sum to the printed $2,501,226 exactly, and cattle, horses, mules, swine and sheep each sum from their own age and sex classes; off the farms the five values sum to $350,736 exactly. The colonies-of- bees value is damaged on this scan and was recovered as $2,561 from the property total, an identity that closes exactly in the neighbouring county column. County totals are added here. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: driveable road centerline in Allen County

points.label: Roads in Allen County, 2010–2024
points.method: The 2024 TIGER/Line road file for county 39003, projected to EPSG:6549 — Ohio North, US survey feet — and summed by feature class. Driveable is the six classes a car can use: primary, secondary, local, vehicular trail, ramp and service drive. Alleys, private service roads, parking-lot roads and the Bureau's internal class are excluded and stated separately. Municipal and township figures are the length of each segment's intersection with the 2024 place and county-subdivision polygons, so a road on a township line is counted in both and the parts sum to more than the whole. The projection was checked before any length was computed, by projecting the county polygon and comparing its area to the published one: agreement to 0.01 per cent. [verified] Every figure is centerline and not route mileage. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: drug overdose deaths, Allen County, twelve months ending

points.label: Drug overdose deaths in Allen County, 2020–2025
points.method: Pulled from the publisher's Socrata endpoint filtered on FIPS 39003, seventy-two rows, no suppression: the county's counts run from 16 to 54 and the withholding threshold is ten. Every row is a twelve-month-ending total, so consecutive rows overlap by eleven months and no two may be added. Ohio and national figures are taken from the publisher's separate state file rather than by summing county rows, because the number of Ohio counties reporting falls from 73 to 45 across this period as counties drop below the threshold, which would invent a decline. Counts are provisional. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: elected county officers named, 1831–1906

points.label: Allen County's officers, 1831–1906
points.method: Read from the full text of the 1906 county history on archive.org, the section headed "Roster of County Officials", transcribed by hand rather than parsed: the scan carries OCR damage in the years — 1S41 for 1841, 1833 where 1853 is meant — and a parser that trusted the digits would have produced a false succession. Each name-and-year pair is the book's; where a year is impossible it is reported as the book's and corrected only against an independent list, never inferred. The count of 169 is the nine offices summed and excludes the associate judges before 1851 and the commissioners. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: enrolment in the county's twelve school districts

points.label: Enrolment in Allen County's twelve school districts, 1988–2024
points.method: One request per year to the district enrolment endpoint for Ohio, `grade-99` and race code 99, filtered here to the twelve districts by NCES agency identifier. Every year from 1988 to 2024 returns all twelve; none is imputed and none is missing. [verified] The twelve are the districts holding ground in Allen County, three of which the federal file files under a neighbouring county — Delphos under Van Wert, Columbus Grove and Pandora-Gilboa under Putnam, Waynesfield-Goshen under Auglaize — so a filter on county code returns eight and not twelve. Staffing is the 2023 district directory, which is the fall of the 2023–24 school year and one year later than the fall the finance survey would call 2024. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: facilities filing a TRI reporting form, Allen County

points.label: Allen County facilities reporting to the Toxics Release Inventory, 1987–2024
points.method: The Envirofacts facility register for Allen County joined to `tri_reporting_form`, paged at 1,000 rows — 5,372 forms across 49 facility identifiers, reporting years 1987 to 2024. A facility is counted as filing in a year if any form carries that year. One register entry, Heat Treating Tech Inc, has no forms at all. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: farms, farm acreage and value of farm property, Allen County

points.label: Allen County farms and farm property, 1900–1910
points.method: Thirteenth Census of Agriculture, enumerated April 15, 1910, with 1900 comparatives printed in italics. Read from rendered images of a 400-dpi scan. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: the three tenure classes of Table 2 sum to Table 1's farm count, acreage, improved acreage and land-and-buildings value independently; the ten size classes sum to 2,939; improved plus woodland plus other unimproved sums to land in farms; the four property components sum to the total in both years; and all six printed averages and percentages recompute. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: farms, land in farms and value of products sold, Allen County

points.label: Allen County farms, farmland and farm income, 2002–2022
points.method: Census of Agriculture, taken for the 2022 calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which agrees on every headline figure. The four tenure rows sum to land in farms exactly and the two sales components sum to the total exactly. NASS defines a farm as "any place from which $1,000 or more of agricultural products were produced and sold, or normally would have been sold, during the census year", which is not the definition the 1910 census used. [verified] See [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml).

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal-aid highway centerline in Allen County

points.label: The federal-aid highways of Allen County, 2018
points.method: The Ohio 2018 HPMS public release feature layer, queried on `county_code=3` and paged at 2,000 rows. Section length is `end_point` minus `begin_point`, which the file states in miles along the route; the sections were checked for overlap by taking the union of the intervals per route before any mileage was summed. Vehicle-miles are `aadt` times section length, summed. Route class is characters five and six of `route_id`. These are route miles and not centerline miles: the same interstate is 46.31 miles in the Census Bureau's linework, and the difference is the subject of [a centerline is not a road](../../decisions/a-centerline-is-not-a-road.yml). [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal disaster and emergency declarations naming Allen County

points.label: Allen County's federal disaster declarations, 1965–2020
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA v2 API filtered to `fipsStateCode` 39 and `fipsCountyCode` 003, and counted here. The `as_of` is the last declaration and not the query date: this file grows, and the figure is a count of what had happened by then. Distinct incidents are counted by grouping rows on the incident window, which merges 2012's pair and 2020's and separates the two of 2004 and 2005. Incident dates before 2004 are not usable — the 1965 and 1978 rows give an incident beginning and ending on the day the declaration was signed. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal hazard mitigation projects recorded for Allen County

points.label: Allen County's federal hazard mitigation, 2003–2026
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA hazard mitigation assistance projects endpoint filtered to state Ohio and county "Allen" — the short spelling, where the public assistance endpoint requires "Allen County". `as_of` is the last close-out date in the file. The federal share for the denied project is null rather than zero and is printed as absent, because a project that was never obligated is not a project obligated at nothing. Dollars are nominal across twenty-two years and are not summed. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal individual and household assistance approved in Allen County

points.label: Federal aid to Allen County households, 2007 and 2020
points.method: Two endpoints, owners and renters, filtered to state OH and county "Allen (County)" — a third spelling of the county on the same API — and summed here. `value` is the two disasters' approved IHP amounts added: $641,634 for 2007 and $3,595,938 for 2020, in nominal dollars thirteen years apart, which is a total and not a comparable one. Registrations are `validRegistrations` and are not households: a household that registers and is found ineligible is counted here. The two endpoints carry different fields — owners have an inspected-damage dollar figure and renters have damage bands — so no damage total is computed across both. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal money for work and payments performed in Allen County

points.label: Federal money in Allen County, 2008–2025
points.method: USAspending's geography endpoint for county 39003, one request per federal year from 2008 to 2025 and per award-type group — contracts, grants, direct payments, loans and other — run twice, once with `scope: place_of_performance` and once with `scope: recipient_location`. A federal year runs 1 October to 30 September and is named for the year it ends in. Every figure in this node is place of performance unless the sentence says otherwise, and the two totals are never added together. Assistance listings and agencies come from the category endpoint with the same county filter. The service serves nothing earlier than 1 October 2007, so 2008 is the first complete year. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federal share obligated for public assistance projects in Allen County

points.label: Federal disaster assistance to Allen County, 2005–2025
points.method: Fetched from the OpenFEMA public assistance funded projects endpoint filtered to `stateAbbreviation` OH and `county` "Allen County" — the longer spelling, which this dataset requires and the declarations dataset does not — and summed here. The `as_of` is the last obligation date in the file and not the query date: this file grows. Dollars are nominal and span twenty years, so the four declaration rows above are not comparable to one another as amounts of purchasing power. The applicant count is of distinct `applicantId`s and treats the two Delphos registrations as two, because the file does. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: federally subsidized housing units

points.label: Federally subsidized housing in Allen County, 2005–2025
points.method: HUD's county, place and housing authority files, Allen County code 39003, Lima place code 3943554, authority OH044, `Summary of All HUD Programs` rows unless a programme is named. Every row is stamped `31DEC2025`. The five programme rows sum to 2,251 units exactly; their occupied counts sum to 2,000 against a published 1,999 and their people counts to 4,219 against a published 4,266, and the file explains neither residual. [verified] The 2005–2008 editions report `hh_income` in thousands and are converted here; their `total_units` is suppressed, which is why the unit series begins in 2009. Rates per thousand use the Vintage 2024 population estimate for every county and for Lima, so that no comparison mixes denominators. Figures taken from HUD's undated map layers are described as retrieved and are not carried into `value` or `as_of`.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: foreign-born white population

points.label: Allen County's foreign-born, 1920
points.method: Read from a page image at 300 dpi. Table 12 splits the countries into two blocks, each of which restarts at Adams County, so Allen's row had to be read from two pages three apart and rejoined; the check that it was rejoined correctly is that the twenty-two figures sum to the printed total of 2,753. Country names are the census's own for 1920 — Jugo-Slavia, Czechoslovakia and Syria are as printed, and the countries they name had existed for two years, one year and none at all as sovereign states. [verified]

points.label: Allen County's foreign-born, 1930–1950
points.method: Read from page images at 300 dpi. The 1930 and 1940 figures are sums of the printed male and female lines and were checked against the county total; the 1950 figure is printed as a total and its twenty-eight country columns were added independently and came to it exactly. Country names are the census's own for 1950 — Yugoslavia, U.S.S.R. and Eire are as printed, and they are not the names the 1920 table used for the same ground. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: full tax rate, highest taxing district in the county

points.label: Property tax rates in Allen County by taxing district, 2012–2025
points.method: The Auditor's tax rate summary PDF for each tax year 2012 through 2025, extracted with `pdftotext -layout` and parsed by tax set. Tax years 2012–2015 use one column order and 2016 onward another; the parser reads the layout from the page header rather than assuming one. Tax year 2013 prints the district name and its rates on separate lines and needs its own pairing rule. Effective rates are the file's own `RES-AGR EFFECTIVE RATE`, and reduction shares are computed here as one minus the effective rate over the full rate. Tax year 2011 and the five historical volumes are scans and are not read. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: full-time employees of Allen County's local governments

points.label: Allen County's forty-five governments and who works for them, 2022
points.method: `22empid.txt` filtered on FIPS state 39 and FIPS county 003, giving 45 units, joined to `22empst.txt` on the fourteen-character legacy identifier. [verified] Item code 000 is the unit total and the rest are functions; the unit totals are used for every count above and the function table sums item codes across all 45 units. [verified] A unit is assigned to the county it is geographically located in or administered from, which for a district crossing a county line is one county and not both. Delphos City Schools and Bluffton Exempted Village Schools serve ground in Van Wert and Hancock counties and are counted here whole. [inference] Employment is a March count and payroll a 31-day March equivalent; neither is annualised here. [verified] Seven units carry imputation flag G on their full-time employment and two carry T; those figures are named above rather than removed. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: full-time-equivalent psychiatrists serving the low-income population, Catchment Area 62

points.label: Allen County's health professional shortage designations, 1985–2026
points.method: The three discipline files filtered on `State and County Federal Information Processing Standard Code` equal to `39003`, deduplicated by `HPSA ID`, which is one row per designation rather than one per component geography. [verified] The three-digit `County or County Equivalent` field is not the county key and matches every third county in the country. [verified] Populations, ratios, full-time equivalents and shortages are the register's own fields as of each row's last update date, which is later than its designation date for every live row here. A figure in a withdrawn row is the figure that stood when it was withdrawn. [verified] The count of fifteen is distinct `HPSA ID` values across the three files: five in primary care, four in dental, six in mental health. Two mental health designations for the same institution, made in March 2021 and March 2022 for different populations, are both live and are counted separately. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: government jobs in Allen County, all ownerships

points.label: Who works for a government in Allen County, 2014–2024
points.method: Annual-average county files for 39003, 2014 through 2024. Aggregation level 70 is the county total across all ownerships and 71 the county by ownership; 73 is ownership by supersector and 74 to 78 by NAICS sector down to six digits. [verified] Government is ownership codes 1, 2 and 3 summed; the file publishes no such total and every government figure here is computed. [inference] Employment is an annual average of monthly counts of jobs covered by unemployment insurance, so a person with two jobs is counted twice and a job not covered is not counted at all. [verified] `avg_annual_pay` is total annual wages divided by annual average employment, which is a wage per job and not a salary. [verified] Named NAICS figures are for 2023 unless stated; the 2024 file agrees with them to within a few employees in every case. [verified] No establishment is named by this file, and the two attributions made above are the corpus's own. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: heart disease death rate, ages 35 and over, Allen County

points.label: Allen County heart disease and stroke mortality, 1999–2024
points.method: Read from CDC's Socrata endpoints by `locationid` = `39003`. Ranks are computed over the 88 Ohio county rows of the same file, stratum and year, sorted worst first; where a county has no estimate it is excluded and the denominator is stated. The twenty-year file names this county `Allen` and the recent vintages name it `Allen County`, and a first ranking pass written for one and run against the other returned 88 counties with this one absent and raised nothing. Trend percentages are the programme's own fitted values from its `1999 - 2010` and `2010 - 2019` rows, not endpoint arithmetic: computing the 1999-to-2010 change from the endpoints gives −26.2 per cent where the file publishes −29.8, and the file's figure is the one quoted. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: high-school pupils enrolled in a dual-enrolment college course

points.label: College Credit Plus in Allen County, 2017 and 2021
points.method: Rates divide by the collection's own enrolment, not the district files'. [verified] The ten schools are the buildings in Allen County with a twelfth grade and a positive enrolment, matched by the school identifier rather than the district's. [verified] West Central Learning Academy is excluded from the county rate's numerator and denominator because it reports that it offers no dual enrolment, which the file records as a reserved code rather than as a zero; Bath is included, because its row says it offers the programme and enrols none. [verified] The 2017 figure omits Apollo Career Center and Perry, whose 2017 rows carry a reserved code, so the 458-to-492 comparison is between two totals over slightly different sets of schools and is not a like-for-like change. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: high schools offering an Advanced Placement course
series.unit: of ten high schools in Allen County, 2021–22

points.label: What Allen County's high schools offer, 2013–2021
points.method: The ten schools are the buildings inside Allen County whose highest grade offered is 12 and whose enrolment is above zero, taken from the district directory for 2021–22 and matched to the collection by the school's own identifier rather than the district's, which is blank in the 2020 vintage. [verified] The Ohio comparison uses the same two rules over every school in the state, which gives 1,009 high schools of which 1,001 answer the AP question. [verified] A school counts as offering a subject when it reports one class of it or more; the class counts are read only from 2017 onward, because the question changed between 2015 and 2017 and every high school in this county jumps at that boundary. [verified] The certified-teacher share is the sum of classes taught by a certified teacher over the sum of classes held, across algebra I, algebra II, geometry, advanced mathematics, calculus, biology, chemistry and physics, skipping subjects a school does not hold. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: highway bridges in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's bridges, 2025
points.method: Selected from the 2025 Ohio delimited file on `COUNTY_CODE_003` = 3 and counted here. "Poor" is the minimum of items 58, 59, 60 and 62 being 4 or less, which is the Federal Highway Administration's own rule; structures with no rating in any of the four are not counted either way, and there were none. The count is of structures in the county whatever the owner, which is not the same as the count of bridges the county maintains. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: highway bridges in poor condition by owner, Allen County

points.label: Allen County bridge condition by owner, 1992–2025
points.method: Twelve editions of the Ohio delimited file, selected on `COUNTY_CODE_003` = 3 and on `RECORD_TYPE_005A` = 1. That second filter is necessary and was not needed for the 2025 edition alone: the older files carry a second row for some structures describing the route beneath them, and 1992 has 436 rows for 393 bridges. Counting rows rather than structures would have invented a fall of seventy-two bridges that did not happen. [verified] "Poor" is the minimum of items 58, 59, 60 and 62 being 4 or less, the Federal Highway Administration's own rule, applied identically in every edition. Structures are linked across editions on `STRUCTURE_NUMBER_008`, which Ohio reassigns when a bridge is replaced, so a replacement appears as a disappearance and a new number rather than as a changed row. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: hours worked, active limestone quarries

points.label: Allen County's quarries, 2000–2025
points.method: Mines with `STATE` = OH and `FIPS_CNTY_NM` beginning ALLEN, six in all. Employment is the mean of the four quarterly `AVG_EMPLOYEE_CNT` values; hours are their sum. 2026 is excluded from every total because only two quarters are filed. Injuries exclude the two records whose degree is `ACCIDENT ONLY` and the one with none. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: house price index, all transactions, and its value in 1975 dollars
