points.label: House prices in Allen County, 1975–2025
points.method: The annual county file, read for FIPS 39003, using the first-recorded-base column so that 1975 is 100. [verified] Real values divide the index by the ratio of the national CPI-U annual average for the year to its 1975 average of 53.8, and are labelled *in 1975 dollars* rather than as any statement about what a house costs. [verified] The national line is the agency's quarterly all-transactions series for the United States, averaged over four quarters, deflated the same way, and read at 2025, the last year with four quarters in it. [verified] The national and Ohio rankings use only the 419 counties with an index in both endpoint years, and the count of counties below their 1975 level is over that same 419. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: household type, multigenerational and coupled households by county subdivision

points.label: Allen County households by township and city, 2020
points.method: Records are selected from the state file's geographic header by summary level and geographic component: 050 with component 00 for the county, 060 with component 00 for each of the thirteen subdivisions, 01 and 43 for the county's urban and rural parts. [verified] A subdivision record and a place record for Lima carry identical household figures and only the subdivision record is used, so the city is counted once. [verified] Cell positions come from the file's own table matrix: a segment's fields are its matrix rows in matrix order, offset by the five that repeat the file identification and the logical record number. [verified] Household type is segment 13, the presence and children tables segment 15, multigenerational households segment 38, coupled and nonfamily households segment 39. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: household type, size, marital arrangement and family poverty

points.label: Who lives with whom in Allen County, 2019–2023
points.method: Every figure is the 2019–2023 five-year estimate for summary level 050, geography `0500000US39003`, except the Lima rows, which are the place record `1600000US3943554` — a figure identical in this file to the county-subdivision record for Lima city. [verified] Shares of a total are computed from the two estimates and their margin from the Bureau's formula for a proportion, which subtracts the numerator's share of the denominator's variance rather than adding the two margins in quadrature. [verified] The county-less-Lima figures are differences of two estimates from the same table and carry no margin here; they are marked as inference for that reason. [verified] The rank across Ohio's counties is a rank of point estimates and no margin was propagated through it. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: households, household type and household size

points.label: Allen County households and household type, 1970–2023
points.method: The 1970 to 2010 rows come from the compendium's complete-count items, not its sample items: the same census years appear twice in that table, from the short form and the long form, and they differ by up to 105 households in this county. [verified] The 2020 row is read from the characteristics file by logical record number, taking the county's summary-level 050 record with geographic component 00. [verified] Persons per household is the file's own item for 1970 to 2010 and is computed for 2020 as persons in households over households, which reproduces the published figure to three decimals at every year where both exist. [verified] The counterfactual household count divides 2020's persons in households by 1970's persons per household, using the unrounded 3.1996 rather than the published 3.20. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: households paying more than 30 per cent of income for housing

points.label: Housing cost burden in Allen County, 2006–2022
points.method: HUD CHAS county files for 2006–2010, 2011–2015, 2015–2019 and 2018–2022, Ohio state code 39 and county code 003, plus the 2018–2022 place file for Lima. Burden counts are the sum of the five income bands' `greater than 30%` and `greater than 50%` cells in Table 8 — for renters the columns based at `T8_est69`, for owners at `T8_est3` — and the denominators are the file's own published tenure totals, which differ from the sum of its rounded parts by a handful of households. [verified] Margins are the root of the sum of squares of the file's own `moe` columns, and a share's margin uses the Census proportion formula. The state and national rates are sums over every county row in the same file. The affordability ratios add Table 14B's vacant-for-rent units to Table 15C's occupied ones, which is how the shortage is normally measured. `value` is the county's owner and renter burdened households added, 3,905 and 4,725, for the 2018–2022 window only.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: housing units, occupancy status, tenure, median value and median gross rent

points.label: Allen County housing units, occupancy, tenure and value, 2023
points.method: Tables B25002, B25003, B25077 and B25064 of the 2023 five-year file, joined on `GEO_ID`. Shares are computed here and medians are published. [verified] Owner-occupancy is of *occupied* units, so its denominator is 40,928 and not 44,697.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: housing units by year structure built (B25034) and median year built (B25035)

points.label: When Allen County's housing was built, 2023
points.method: Shares are computed here from published counts; the medians are published. [verified] The bands describe *surviving* housing, so a low count for an early decade is demolition and construction together and cannot be read as construction alone. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: housing units in Allen County lacking complete plumbing facilities

points.label: What is in Allen County's houses, 2023
points.method: Table-based summary file, 2019–2023 five-year estimates, tables B25047 and B25051 over all housing units and B25049, B25053, B25040, B25044 and B25014 over occupied ones. [verified] The vacant-unit figures are the all-units table less the occupied-units table cell by cell, which the survey does not publish; their margins are the two margins in quadrature. [inference] Shares outside Lima are the county row less the Lima city subdivision row, and the thirteen subdivisions close against the county in every table used here. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: interurban railway companies serving Lima

points.label: Allen County's interurban railways, 1901–1921
points.method: Read from the transportation, township and county chapters of the 1906 history, the 1921 history, and the 1917 federal directory. The 1905 figure of three counts names printed in one chapter; a fourth name appears in another chapter of the same book and is not added, because nothing establishes that it is a fourth company rather than a fourth name. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: itemized federal contributions from Allen County residents, 2023–24 cycle

points.label: Federal campaign contributions from Allen County, 1980–2024
points.method: The Commission's `indiv` bulk file for each of twelve presidential cycles, streamed and filtered on the fly to records whose state is OH and whose ZIP begins 458, then reduced to Allen County three ways. [verified] *Deduplicated.* From 2012 the archive holds `itcont.txt` and a `by_date/` partition of the same records, so every `SUB_ID` appears exactly twice; and a conduit files the money it passes on as a `24T` while the committee that receives it files the same contributor, date and amount as a `15E`, a `15` or a `10`. Reading the 2024 archive without either step gives $1,528,070 against $611,489 — two and a half times the figure. A `24T` is kept only where no other row carries the same contributor, date and amount. [verified] *Netted.* Refunds to contributors, transaction type `22Y`, carry positive amounts in this file and are subtracted. [verified] *Weighted.* Each record is multiplied by the share of its ZIP code tabulation area's population that lives in Allen County, from [the crosswalk](allen-county-zip-codes-2020.yml). Under the three alternative rules the 2024 total is $454,593 for the eight wholly-inside codes, $650,446 for the thirteen majority-Allen codes and $959,382 for every code that touches the county at all. [verified] A conduit's pass-through is attributed to the committee named in `OTHER_ID` rather than to the conduit, because WinRed writes no memo text where ActBlue writes a parseable one and both populate that field. Party comes from the committee master where it is filled and from the candidate master through the committee's candidate where it is not; committees with neither are reported as unlabelled rather than guessed at. [verified] Donors are distinct contributor names within a ZIP within a cycle, which merges two people of the same name at the same post office and separates one person who moved. [inference] No individual contributor is named anywhere in this corpus; employers and occupations are recorded because they are properties of firms and of work.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: jobs in Allen County, all occupations

points.label: Allen County occupations and wages, 2014 and 2024
points.method: Read from the May 2024 and May 2014 metropolitan workbooks by `AREA` = 30620, parsed from the spreadsheets' XML parts because no spreadsheet library is installed. The two headers differ — `AREA` is the first column in 2024 and the second in 2014, the location quotient is `LOC_QUOTIENT` and `LOC QUOTIENT`, the group column `O_GROUP` and `OCC_GROUP` — and a reader written for one returns zero rows against the other with no error, which it did before the column was looked up by name. Location quotients are the file's own. Major-group changes across the two vintages were checked occupation by occupation for codes present in one year and absent in the other before any difference was written down. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: jobs located in the county, and where their holders live

points.label: Who comes and goes to work in Allen County, 2022
points.method: LODES8 origin-destination files for Ohio, `JT00` — all jobs — for 2022, filtered to origin-destination pairs with a block in Allen County on either end, plus the auxiliary file for workers living outside Ohio. Counties are read from the first five digits of a block identifier and "Lima" from the tract whose internal point falls inside the city's 2020 boundary, which is a statement about where a tract's centre is. Earnings bands are the file's own `SE01`, `SE02` and `SE03`. Every total here is a sum over thousands of cells; no cell is quoted. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land area

points.label: Allen County land area, 2020
points.method: Computed by the Census Bureau from the 2020 TIGER geography. A county's land area is not fixed across geographies — a later vintage may differ. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land area by county subdivision

points.label: Allen County land area by subdivision, 2000–2024
points.method: Land and total area for all thirteen Allen County subdivisions read from the county-subdivision tables of the 2000 and 2010 Population and Housing Unit Counts volumes for Ohio, both born digital and extracted exactly rather than by OCR; annual figures from the Ohio place, county-subdivision and county gazetteer files for 2012 through 2024, converted from square metres at 2,589,988.11 m² to the square mile and 4,046.8564224 m² to the acre. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land in farms

points.label: Allen County farms, 1949–1987
points.method: Read off page images rendered at 400 dpi from the two archive.org scans, because the text layers of both volumes are unusable — the 1987 PDF drops its numeric grid entirely and the djvu text of both delivers digits as an unaligned stream. The headline value is 1954's because it is the figure the four-year fall lands on and the one most heavily cross-checked. Each figure was verified against another in the same column: an acreage against the farm count and the printed average, and an acreage against the printed proportion in farms. The 1950 and 1982 columns are taken from the 1954 and 1987 volumes respectively rather than from the censuses of those years, which is what makes each pair internally comparable. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land in farms, Allen County

points.label: Land in farms, Allen County, 1910–2022
points.method: Every figure between 1920 and 1978 read from a 300-dpi render of the page, never from the text layer, which mangles digits in these typefaces — it gives Ohio's 1920 land in farms as 23,615,888 where the page prints 23,515,888 and its 1910 farm count as 272,046 against a printed 272,045. Land area, and so the percentage in farms, is not constant across the run: the volumes give the county 259,840 acres in 1925, 262,400 in 1940, 1945, 1959 and 1964, and 262,405 in 1969, so acreage rather than share is what this node compares. Farm counts are not comparable across the definition changes of 1959, 1974 and 1978; see [a farm count is a definition](../../decisions/a-farm-count-is-a-definition.yml). [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land in the special flood hazard area

points.label: The mapped floodplain of Allen County, 2026
points.method: Layer 28 of the National Flood Hazard Layer, `DFIRM_ID='39003C'`, taken in seven pages of 250 with retries and projected to EPSG:26916 on the server. Polygons flagged `SFHA_TF = 'T'` were unioned and the union intersected with the 2024 TIGER county polygon; the zone table is each polygon intersected with the county and summed by `FLD_ZONE` and `ZONE_SUBTY`, and it accounts for 99.97 per cent of the county's area, the remainder being ground the FIRM does not cover. [verified] Township and place shares are the union intersected with each polygon, divided by that polygon's own area inside this county. [verified] Population and housing are `POP20` and `HOUSING20` on the 2020 blocks, reported as three figures — blocks wholly inside, blocks weighted by area, and blocks touching — rather than as one. [inference] Acres are 4046.8564224 square metres.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: land poorly drained or worse

points.label: The soils of Allen County
points.method: One Soil Data Access query joining `legend`, `mapunit` and `component` on `areasymbol = 'OH003'`, returning 436 rows. [verified] Every share is acres weighted by component share of map unit — `muacres` times `comppct_r` over 100 — because a map unit is a mixture and its rating is not a single value. The alternatives are recorded in the catalogue and are not used. `as_of` is the survey's own restoration date of 27 August 2025; its field lineage runs from 1965. Drainage, hydric and taxonomic shares come from the component table and the prime-farmland share from the map-unit table, which is why the second is a share of map-unit acres rather than of components.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: law enforcement agencies reporting for Allen County

points.label: Allen County's reporting police agencies, 2026
points.method: Read from the Ohio agency list, selecting the county key ALLEN, which is the FBI's own assignment and not a geographic test — an agency serving two counties appears under a combined key and would be missed here. Dates are the file's `nibrs_start_date` verbatim. The population figures are each agency's own service population, which is not a census figure and does not sum to the county. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: layoff notices naming a union, Allen County

points.label: Unions named in Allen County layoff notices, 1996–2017
points.method: The register's `Union` column, read as printed. Blank, `None`, `N/A` and `n/a` are all treated as naming no union and are not distinguished, because the files use them interchangeably across years and no key explains the difference. `USWA` and `United Steelworkers` are counted as one. `AFL-CIO` is counted as a naming, though it identifies a federation and not a bargaining unit. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: life expectancy at birth, Allen County

points.label: What Allen County dies of early, 2016–2022
points.method: Read from the publisher's 2025 annual release CSV, one row for Allen County and one each for Ohio and the United States, taking the `_rawvalue`, `_numerator` and race-specific columns. The data years are from the publisher's technical documentation, which the CSV does not carry, and they differ by measure — three years for premature death and overdoses, five for suicides and firearms, seven for homicides and motor vehicle deaths. Counts are the numerator column, which holds deaths rather than the years of potential life lost the codebook claims. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: life expectancy at birth, by census tract
series.unit: years between the county's highest and lowest tract

points.label: Life expectancy at birth in Allen County's census tracts, 2010–2015
points.method: NCHS estimates for 2010–2015, on 2010 census tracts. The join to Lima is by tract identifier to the 2020 tract file and then by that tract's published internal point against the city's 2020 boundary polygon — so it is a statement about where a tract's centre falls and not about how many of its people live in the city. Two of the thirty tracts have no 2020 identifier and are excluded from every comparison, and are in the range and the median. Medians and weighted means are this corpus's arithmetic; every input is NCHS's or the Census Bureau's. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: livestock inventory, Allen County

points.label: Allen County livestock, 2002–2022
points.method: Census of Agriculture, inventory taken at December 31 of the census year and sales for the calendar year, read from NASS's Quick Stats bulk county file and checked against the published county profile, which prints the same 2022 and 2017 inventories. `(D)` marks a cell NASS suppressed to avoid disclosing an individual operation and is not a small number; nothing here infers a value for one. Comparisons to 1910 set a count of animals on farms and off them against a count on farms alone, which in 1910 differed by about one per cent for swine. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: local ballot questions put to Allen County voters

points.label: What Allen County was asked on the ballot, 2003–2012
points.method: Ninety category reports — tax, bond, misc, combined, school issues, income tax — for sixteen election days, parsed here. Two layouts: through 2004 the millage and purpose come first with the votes on the first line and the subdivision named after; from 2005 the subdivision comes first with the votes beside it. Both are handled and the boundary was found by inspection. [verified] Questions are de-duplicated on election date and vote totals, because a ballot question that combines a bond and a levy is printed in both category reports with identical figures; the Secretary's own summary tables count those as two or three issues and this node counts the question. [verified] Everything filed under any of the other eighty-seven counties whose subdivision names Allen in its parenthetical is included. [verified] Levy type is the word the ballot uses — renewal, replacement, additional — taken from the description, and is absent for five questions whose wording gives no such word. [inference] Passage is a simple majority of the votes reported, which is the rule the reports print at the head of every page; the 57-to-57 return is counted as a failure on that rule. [inference] Every figure here is a count of questions or a share of votes within one question. No vote totals are summed across questions or attributed to this county. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: local option liquor questions decided in Allen County

points.label: Local option liquor elections in Allen County, 2003–2012
points.method: Sixteen local option reports, 2003 through 2012, parsed here. Their layout is not the layout of the other issue reports: a county name on the first row of its block and blank thereafter, then the precinct or establishment, then the form code, then the yes and no columns. Rows are attributed to Allen County by carrying the last county name seen. [verified] Thirty questions carry returns and two do not; the two are November 2003, whose report is a list of certified questions rather than a result. [verified] The March 2004 report's own title names the wrong election and its contents are confirmed against the Secretary's summary table for that date. [verified] Establishments are named because the source names them and they are businesses and veterans' posts rather than people. [inference] Passage is a simple majority of the votes reported. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: low birthweight, prematurity, fertility and infant mortality

points.label: Birth outcomes in Allen County, 2000–2021
points.method: Measures 36 and 1416 (percent low birthweight), 30 and 1412 (percent preterm), 35 and 1415 and 29 and 1411 (the counts), 45 and 1425 (fertility rate) and 279 (infant mortality), all at stratification level 2 for FIPS 39003 and for Ohio. [verified] Where a measure exists in two variants the table above reads the pre-2018 variant through 2020 and the 2018-onward variant for 2021, and the two are never averaged. [verified] Infant mortality is a five-year rate labelled by its final year, so its 2020 figure covers 2016–2020 and is not comparable year to year with the single-year measures beside it. [verified] Low birthweight and prematurity are singleton births only, which is the publisher's definition and excludes the twins in whom both are commonest. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employees, Allen County

points.label: Allen County manufactures, 1939–1967
points.method: Census of Manufactures, taken for the calendar years 1939, 1947, 1954, 1958, 1963 and 1967 and read from page images of five archive.org scans; none of the five has a usable text layer for tables. Establishments are those inside the county, on a $5,000 minimum through 1939 and on the Bureau's later size rules afterwards. Four population columns printed beside the manufacturing figures — 73,303 and 44,711 for 1940, 88,183 and 50,246 for 1950 — reproduce census counts this corpus already holds, and were checked before any figure here was written down. The 1967 volume's Lima area row equals the sum of Allen, Putnam and Van Wert in eleven of twelve columns exactly. [verified] The 1958 figure is printed three times and not identically: 13,526 in the 1958 volume, 13,534 in the 1963 volume's retrospective column, and 13,543 in that volume's row for the same area under its other name. This node takes the 1958 volume's own. The spread is seventeen people. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employees outside the city of Lima, Allen County

points.label: Allen County manufacturing outside Lima, 1929–1967
points.method: Seven subtractions of a city row from a county row of the same table on the same page of the same volume, which is what makes them safe: the two rows share a census, a definition and a printing. 1929 is wage earners from the 1929 state chapter, 1939 wage earners from the 1939 one, and 1947 to 1967 all employees from the area statistics volumes. The 1967 pair is printed in thousands to one decimal, so its difference is good to about a hundred people either way. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employment, Allen County, all jobs

points.label: Allen County manufacturing employment, 1969–2022
points.method: BEA CAEMP25S for 1969–2000 (SIC line 400) and CAEMP25N for 2001–2022 (NAICS line 500), read from the Ohio county files at GeoFIPS 39003. BEA counts jobs, including proprietors, part-time work, farm and government, where County Business Patterns counts employees of private establishments; the two are separate programmes and not one series. They agree on shape where they overlap, both placing the recent trough at the end of the 2000s and a recovery of about a fifth since. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing employment, Allen County, private employers

points.label: Allen County manufacturing employment, 1986–2023
points.method: County Business Patterns county files, every year from 1986 to 2023 — the nine-year sample this node was built on has been replaced by the full annual run, and none of the nine figures moved. Checked by arithmetic self-closure: in 1986 the ten SIC divisions sum to the printed county total exactly, and in 2022 the twenty NAICS sectors do the same. Years between leave residuals of 2 to 239, each year carrying at least one sector with suppressed employment. Corroborated at the recent end by [the QCEW](../../catalog/bls-qcew.md), which gives 8,661 for 2023 against 8,573 for 2022. Government, the self-employed and farms are excluded throughout. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: manufacturing wage earners, Allen County

points.label: Allen County manufactures, 1929
points.method: Read from a page image at 300 dpi; the volume has no text layer. The row was checked three ways before it was written down: the cost of materials and containers plus the cost of fuel and purchased energy equals the printed total cost, the value of products less that total equals the printed value added, and the population column prints 69,419, which is the 1930 count this corpus already holds from three other volumes. The scan renders the value of products as 47,130,403; the two identities require 47,139,403 and every other row on the page closes them exactly. Establishments here are those reporting products of $5,000 or more, which is not the basis used before 1921. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: mapped stream channel in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's stream network, 2026
points.method: NetworkNHDFlowline features intersecting the envelope −84.42,40.62 to −83.86,40.94, taken as GeoJSON in two pages of a thousand and clipped to the 2024 TIGER county polygon in EPSG:26916. 1,792 flowlines intersect the envelope and 1,150 have length inside the county. Every mile here is clipped length, not the reach's own `LengthKm`. [verified] Class counts are of reaches with any length inside the county, so a reach crossing the line is counted once in its class and contributes only its inside miles. [verified] The trunk assignment walks `levelpathi` and `dnhydroseq` downstream from each reach to the first level path whose reaches are named for a trunk, and is read from reaches rather than paths. [verified] — see [a level path is not a river](../../decisions/a-level-path-is-not-a-river.yml).

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: marital status of the population 15 years and over, by sex
series.unit: people now married, of 82,015 aged 15 and over

points.label: Marital status in Allen County, 2019–2023
points.method: The universe of B12001 is the total population fifteen and over, which includes people in group quarters — the two state prisons in this county among them — and so is not the same universe as the household tables beside it. [verified] Shares are computed over the sex-specific totals the table publishes rather than over the county's population. [verified] The margin on a difference of two estimates is the root of the sum of their squares, which the Bureau's own guidance gives and which is conservative where the two are drawn from the same sample. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: median age (B01002) and population by age (B01001)

points.label: Allen County age structure, 2023
points.method: 2023 five-year estimates. Under-18 sums B01001 male 3-6 and female 27-30; 65-and-over sums male 20-25 and female 44-49. The twelve townships and Lima sum to the county's 101,685. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: median household income (B19013) and poverty status (B17001)

points.label: Allen County household income and poverty, 2023
points.method: 2023 five-year estimates from the table-based summary file. The twelve townships and Lima are county-subdivision and place summary levels and partition the county: they sum to 101,685 people and 12,815 below poverty, both equal to the county row. The two totals come from different tables with different universes — B01001 counts everybody and B17001 counts the 97,786 for whom poverty status is determined — and a share of one taken over the other is what this node originally published. Margins are as published, at 90 per cent; combined margins are the root of the sum of squares. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: members of the U.S. House named as representing the county, 1831–1906

points.label: Allen County in Congress, 1831–1933
points.method: The 1906 book's list transcribed by hand — the scan runs the district headings into the prose and an automatic reading would lose them, which is where its only error is. The federal record was queried for Ohio districts 3, 4 and 5 for every Congress from 1831 to 1907 and matched to the book by surname within the book's own spans; the two spelling differences the match threw up (Emery for Emory, Le Blond for LeBlond) are the transcriber's and not the record's. The count of eighteen is persons, not entries: Potter and Le Fevre each appear twice under different headings. The federal file is authority for who sat for a district and is not authority for which district this county was in, so no claim here derives the second from the first. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: modelled prevalence of health measures, county and city
series.unit: per cent of Lima adults food insecure, as estimated

points.label: CDC's health estimates for Allen County and Lima, 2022–2023
points.method: Crude prevalence only, because the tract file publishes nothing else and a crude figure must not be set against an age-adjusted one. Thirty-five of the forty measures rest on BRFSS 2023 and five — all teeth lost, dental visits, mammograms, colorectal screening, short sleep — on BRFSS 2022. "Differs by more than the confidence limits allow" means the city's published interval and the county's do not overlap, which is a weaker test than a significance test and is the only one these published fields support. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: mortgage applications acted on, originations, denials and dollars originated
series.unit: applications acted on across seven years

points.label: Allen County mortgage lending, 2018-2024
points.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3 and exclude withdrawn, purchased and incomplete files, as in [the single year](allen-county-home-lending-2023.yml). [verified] "Lima tracts" is the same sixteen of thirty-five used there. Dollar totals are sums of published loan amounts, each rounded to a $10,000 midpoint, so a total of this size carries a rounding band of its own and is quoted to the nearest hundred thousand. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: mortgage applications acted on, originations and denials

points.label: Allen County mortgage applications and denials, 2023
points.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3 — originated, approved and declined, denied — and exclude the 388 withdrawn, 197 purchased and 93 closed for incompleteness, none of which is a decision about a borrower. [verified] "Lima tracts" is the sixteen of the county's thirty-five whose 2020 population is majority Lima; they hold 32,575 of the city's 35,579 people and 3,093 who live outside it. [verified] — [block assignment](../../catalog/census-block-assignment-2020.md). Nine rows carry no tract, seven of them decisions; those seven are in the county's totals and in neither column, which is why the columns sum to 2,599 and not 2,606. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: mortgage denial rate by applicant race, and by race within four controls
series.unit: ratio of observed to expected denials for Black applicants

points.label: Allen County mortgage denial rates by applicant race, 2018-2024
points.method: Rates use actions 1, 2 and 3. Race is the register's `derived_race`; 18 per cent of rows record none and are in no column here. Debt-to-income is grouped from a column that reports integers from 36 to 49 and bands elsewhere. Cells with fewer than ten white applications are dropped, which discards 17 per cent of Black applications rather than resting a rate on one or two files. [verified] Expected denials are the sum of the within-cell white rates over the matched Black applications; the standard deviation is that of the Poisson-binomial they define.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: named features standing on Allen County ground

points.label: Allen County's named features, counted two ways
points.method: The Ohio domestic names file, 17,921 rows, filtered two ways. First on `county_name == "Allen"` and `state_numeric == 39`, which is the filter the catalog entry already documents and which returns 109. Second by ray-casting every Ohio row's primary and source coordinates against the Census Bureau's 2020 county polygon for GEOID 39003, 1,243 vertices, counting a feature if either coordinate falls inside; that returns 120. Distances to the boundary are computed on a local flat-earth approximation and are quoted only to the nearest metre, which is well inside what that approximation supports at this latitude. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: names in the county's two General Assembly rosters

points.label: Allen County in the Ohio General Assembly, 1833–1906
points.method: Both lists transcribed by hand from the full text on archive.org. They are printed as running prose separated by commas, not as tables, and the scan has damage in the names — "Cr.ites" for Crites, "William Ruler" where a Rusler may be meant — so the entries are given as printed and no spelling is corrected against anything. The count of 70 is entries, not persons: three senate names occur twice and one name occurs in both chambers, so the seventy entries are sixty-six people. The assembly counts are inclusive of both endpoints and are floors, since the book postdates the 74th. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: natural population change, four years to 2024

points.label: Allen County natural change, 2021–2024
points.method: Births minus deaths, summed over the four full estimate years 2021–2024. The partial year 2020 — April to June, 293 births and 283 deaths — is excluded as not comparable. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: net migration, four years to 2024

points.label: Allen County net migration, 2021–2024
points.method: Domestic plus international net migration, summed over the four full estimate years 2021–2024. The partial year 2020 is excluded as not comparable. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: net migration exemptions, Allen County, 2004–05 to 2022–23

points.label: Who moved into and out of Allen County, 2004–2023
points.method: Rows where the Allen County side of the pair is FIPS 39/003, taken from `countyoutflow` for departures and `countyinflow` for arrivals. The two files order their FIPS pairs oppositely and the Allen County side is columns one and two in both. [verified] Totals are the rows coded 97/000, *Total Migration-US*; the same-state and different-state splits are 97/001 and 97/003 and the regional residues 59/001 to 59/007. [verified] Non-migrant rows, where origin and destination are both 39/003, are excluded from every figure here. [verified] An exemption is a proxy for a person and a return for a household. Aggregate AGI is in thousands of dollars, nominal, and is the income reported on the returns that moved rather than the income those people had after moving. [verified] No figure here is deflated. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: net migration exemptions to Franklin County, 2004–05 to 2022–23

points.label: Where Allen County's movers went and came from, 2004–2023
points.method: Named flows only: rows whose other side is a real FIPS county code, excluding the summary codes 96, 97, 98, 57, 58 and 59 and excluding the non-migrant row where both sides are 39/003. [verified] Each county's figures are summed across every year in which its flow was published, so a county named in fourteen years and a county named in nineteen are not directly comparable and the year count is stated where it matters. [verified] The nine metropolitan counties are Franklin, Cuyahoga, Hamilton, Montgomery, Lucas, Summit, Delaware, Butler and Warren — every Ohio county holding or bordering a city of over a hundred thousand that appears in this record. The grouping is this corpus's and not the file's. [inference] The two anomalous file years, 2014–15 and 2016–17, are included in these nineteen-year sums because the anomaly is a shift of returns between adjacent years and cancels across the pair. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: new cases filed, all courts of record sitting in the county

points.label: Allen County court caseloads, 2007–2017
points.method: Rows read from the `Overall Caseloads` table of each division and of the municipal courts, in each annual report, by matching the county name `Allen` and the court name `Lima`. The common pleas total is the sum of the four divisions and is computed here; the report publishes no such total. The 2017 value above is that sum plus the municipal court. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: new forcible entry and detainer filings, Lima Municipal Court

points.label: Allen County foreclosures and evictions, 2007–2017
points.method: Foreclosures from the `Foreclosures Overall Caseloads` table of the general division, evictions from the `Forcible Entry and Detainer Overall Caseloads` table of the municipal courts, in each annual report. New filings is the second numeric column in both; the first is cases pending on 1 January, which chains to the previous year's closing balance in all ten transitions. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: newspaper titles recorded as published in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's newspapers, 1843–2026
points.method: The Library of Congress collection endpoint faceted to `location_county:allen` and `location_state:ohio`, `c=200`, which returns all 99 records in one response, followed by the full item record for each of the 99. Place of publication is `location_city` checked against the county's twelve settlements; two records match none of them and are excluded from the 97. Frequency, language and party are read from the item records and not inferred. Holdings are counted as records whose `holding_data.data` is non-empty. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: notices received under sixty days before the layoff, Allen County

points.label: How long before the layoff Ohio received the notice, Allen County, 1996–2017
points.method: Both columns are the register's own: `Date Rcvd` and `Layoff Date`. Where a row gives a range of layoff dates the first date in the range is used, which is the reading most favourable to a long interval; the four rows affected are Lipari Foods in 2012, whose layoff column reads "Beginning 7/1/2012", and three whose ranges begin on the date used here. One row, Lipari Foods, carries no plain layoff date at all and its interval is measured to the beginning of the stated range. No row was excluded. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: occupied housing units, Allen County

points.label: Allen County housing occupancy and household size, 2020
points.method: Table H1, Occupancy Status, from the Ohio file of the 2020 Census Redistricting Data Summary File (P.L. 94-171), file segment 02, the last three fields of each record. Summed from the 3,552 block records for county 39003, joined to the geographic header on LOGRECNO and grouped by the header's county-subdivision code. [verified] Household size is population less group-quarters population, over occupied units, computed here for each subdivision. [inference] It is the definition the Census Bureau uses for average household size, and it is stated here rather than taken from a published table because no published table at this geography is held. Both closures were checked: the thirteen subdivision populations sum to the county's 102,206 and their units to 44,563, with no residual. The same table was later read from the Demographic and Housing Characteristics file and agrees on all 3,552 blocks. [verified] That is not corroboration — the two files are one answer released twice — and it is recorded so that no later reader takes it for one.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: on-site releases of listed toxic chemicals reported by facilities in the county

points.label: Toxic releases reported in Allen County, 1987–2024
points.method: Envirofacts `tri_facility` filtered to Ohio and Allen County, joined to `tri_reporting_form` and `tri_release_qty`, all 55,329 release rows across reporting years 1987–2024. Quantities in grams — 252 rows, 11.5 grams in total, all dioxin — are excluded rather than converted. 1,506 rows carrying a range code instead of a quantity are excluded and could add at most 1.5 million pounds across the whole series. Historical media codes `LANDF8795` and `UNINJ8795` are summed with their replacements after checking that no form carries a nonzero quantity under both. The like-for-like column restricts to chemicals whose dictionary entry has an `active_date` of 1987 or earlier and no `inactive_date`. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: open highway-rail grade crossings

points.label: Allen County's railroads, 2026
points.method: Current Form 71 inventory as of retrieval, filtered to FIPS 39003, counting rows whose `crossingclosed` field is `No`. 95 of the 201 open rows were last revised in 2025 and 92 in 2026; twelve carry revisions from 2014 to 2024 and are stale to that degree. A crossing is a place a road meets a track, so a railroad with many crossings is not necessarily a railroad with much track or much traffic — the train counts are recorded separately and are used here for that. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: owner-occupied housing units, Allen County

points.label: Who owns Allen County's houses, 2010 and 2020
points.method: Table H4 of the 2020 Demographic and Housing Characteristics File, segment 1, data fields 9 to 12, and table H10 at fields 143 to 159; table H4 of 2010 Summary File 1, segment 44, fields 4 to 7, and table H14 at fields 79 to 95. Both joined to their geographic headers on LOGRECNO. [verified] The denominator of every ownership rate here is occupied units, not housing units. [verified] Outside-Lima figures are the county record minus the Lima place record, which is exact because Lima lies wholly inside the county and the two files agree with the thirteen subdivisions' sums. [verified] The 88-county rankings are computed over every county record in the Ohio file. [inference] Occupancy and tenure in the 2020 file are protected figures rather than enumerated ones, and no interval is published for them; the housing-unit totals they sit inside are invariant. [verified] — see [the total is enumerated and the split is not](../../decisions/the-total-is-enumerated-and-the-split-is-not.yml). No claim here rests on a block or on a difference of less than a point.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: paid employees for pay period including March 12, NAICS 62 and its four subsectors

points.label: Allen County health care employment by subsector, 2010–2023
points.method: County files, fipstate 39 fipscty 003. The four subsectors sum to the sector total exactly in all fourteen years, so no line is suppressed. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: paid flood insurance claims in Allen County

points.label: Flood insurance claims in Allen County, 1978–2023
points.method: `NfipClaims` filtered on `countyCode eq '39003'`, all 259 rows taken in one request. Amounts are the sum of the building, contents and increased-cost-of-compliance payments, unadjusted for inflation because the file's own dollars span forty-six years and no single deflator suits a mixture of building and contents payments; see [a deflator is a choice](../../decisions/a-deflator-is-a-choice.yml). [verified] Rates per policy term use `NfipPolicies` filtered on `reportedZipCode`, which is the only county-shaped filter that endpoint accepts, cut to the eight postal areas lying wholly inside this county and to 2009–2026, the years the policy file covers. [verified] A policy term is one row and is not one building. [verified] No coordinate, address or block group from either file is reproduced here.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: people in Ohio state prison committed from Allen County

points.label: People sent to state prison from Allen County, 1983–2019
points.method: `incarceration_trends_county.csv` filtered on `county_fips = 39003`, against the state file for Ohio. Prison figures derive from the National Corrections Reporting Program and are counted by county of commitment on 31 December; they say nothing about where a person is held. [verified] Rates are the file's own, per 100,000 residents aged 15 to 64. [verified] The ratio of population to admissions is reported as that and not as a duration. [inference] Racial shares are computed against the 2020 census count of the county's Black residents alone, 12,573 of 102,206; the alone-or-in-combination count of 15,636 would put the share at 15.3 per cent and the disparity lower. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: people served by community water systems in Allen County

points.label: Allen County's public water systems, 2026
points.method: Selected on the `OH02` identifier prefix, which is Ohio's county code for Allen, and restricted to `pws_activity_code` A and `pws_type_code` CWS. The thirty-three active non-community systems — rest areas, campgrounds, schools, a tavern — are excluded, because they serve people who are passing through or at work and counting them against a resident population would double-count. Populations are as each system reports them and are service populations, not residents of any boundary this corpus holds. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: people under 65 without health insurance, Allen County

points.label: Who in Allen County has no health insurance, 2008–2024
points.method: The Bureau's model estimate, geography category 50, age category 0, race category 0, sex category 0, income category 0, from each year's own file. [verified] County rows carry only race category 0; the seven race categories exist at state level alone. [verified] The denominator is the poverty universe, which excludes people in institutions, in military group quarters and in college dormitories. It is not the survey's universe: the American Community Survey's coverage tables count the civilian noninstitutionalised population, about 2,000 more people under 65 in this county, so the two counts are close and not identical. [inference] The 2013 estimate is the May 2016 revision, the only version in the file taken. [verified] Cells published in 2024 that do not exist in 2008 — age categories 3, 5 and 6 and income category 5 — are not used in any comparison across the whole span. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: people without health insurance, Allen County

points.label: What Allen County's health insurance is made of, 2019–2023
points.method: Table B27001 read as 57 cells — total, then each sex by nine age bands with total, with coverage and without — and B27010 as 66, from the 2019–2023 five-year table-based summary file, geography `0500000US39003` for the county and `1600000US3943554` for Lima. [verified] The universe of both tables is the civilian noninstitutionalised population, so the county's prisons and its nursing home residents are outside it. [verified] Aggregate margins are the square root of the sum of the squared component margins, which is the Bureau's own rule for summed cells. [inference] Coverage counts by kind are not additive with the uninsured: a person holding two kinds appears once, in the combination rows, and the residual rows named "other coverage combinations" are not decomposable. Every figure here that counts a kind of coverage is a floor. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: per capita personal income, and its earnings, property and transfer components

points.label: Personal income in Allen County, 1969–2024
points.method: CAINC4 for totals and the residence adjustment, CAINC30 for per-capita components, both from the January 2026 vintage; the older CAINC35 is used only in [the transfer node](allen-county-transfer-receipts-1969-2024.yml) and never mixed with these. [verified] Real figures divide by the ratio of the national CPI-U annual average for the year to its 2024 average of 313.689, and are labelled *in 2024 dollars*. [verified] Earnings per job divides BEA earnings by place of work by BEA total employment for the same year, which counts part-time and proprietors' jobs as whole jobs, so it is an average over jobs and not a wage. [verified] The employment series ends in 2022 and the earnings-per-job line ends with it. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: personal current transfer receipts, and their composition

points.label: Government transfers to Allen County, 1969–2024
points.method: Totals and the 2024 figure come from CAINC4 line 47, January 2026 vintage; every share and every component figure comes from CAINC35, October 2023 vintage, computed within that file against its own total of $1,373,641,000 rather than against the newer one, which is 3.6 per cent larger. [verified] The two are never mixed inside one ratio. The USAspending figures are the place-of-performance scope summed across all five award-type groups for the federal year, which is the same series [the federal money node](federal-money-in-allen-county-2008-2025.yml) publishes; the assistance listing count is that endpoint paged to exhaustion, 99 rows. [verified] A federal year ends 30 September and a BEA year is a calendar year, so the matched pairs are matched by label and not by period. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: persons admitted in Ohio with an Allen County address of record

points.label: The Allen County roll of Ohio attorneys, 1925–2026
points.method: One POST to the directory's `Ajax.ashx` with `county=Allen` and every other field empty. The response carried `TooManyResults: false`, so the 334 rows are the whole answer at the 1,000-row cap rather than a truncation. The county filter is a substring match and is not scoped to a state; the same query with `state=IN` returns zero rows, which is how these were confirmed to be Ohio addresses and not Fort Wayne's. Counts by status, by decade and by admitted-by are tallies of those rows and nothing is estimated. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: physicians in patient care, Allen County

points.label: Who practises medicine in Allen County, 2022–2024
points.method: County row `39003` of the 2024–2025 release, health professions and health facilities modules, variables carrying the `_23` and `_24` suffixes. [verified] Rates per 100,000 use the file's own `popn_est_23` of 100,838 for the county and the sum of all 88 Ohio county estimates, 11,785,935, for the state, so numerator and denominator come from one file. [inference] Physician counts are non-federal and exclude those aged 75 and over where the variable says so; the primary care count excluding residents also excludes them. [verified] Nurse practitioner, physician assistant and identifier-based dentist counts are registrations with CMS and are flagged in the documentation as needing the user guide; they are not comparable with the masterfile counts and are not summed with them here. [verified] Every variable in this file carries two years and no more. Nothing here is a trend. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population 25 and over with a bachelor's degree or more, Allen County

points.label: Educational attainment in Allen County, 2005–2009 and 2019–2023
points.method: Table B15002, *Sex by Educational Attainment for the Population 25 Years and Over*, from the 2019–2023 and 2005–2009 five-year American Community Survey summary files. The two vintages carry the same thirty-five lines in the same order, so male and female cells are summed pairwise and grouped identically in both. [verified] The 2023 file is table-based and self-describing. The 2009 file is sequence-based: table B15002 is thirty-five cells beginning at position 90 of sequence 40, the geography is joined on a seven-character logical record number at column 14 of a separate fixed-width file, and neither file names a variable. [verified] Shares are ratio estimates and their margins are computed as the Census Bureau directs, with the denominator's variance subtracted where the result stays positive and added where it does not. A difference is called only where it exceeds the root sum of squares of the two margins, at the 90 per cent level the Bureau publishes. [verified] The national row is 2023 only; the 2009 state file holds Ohio and its subdivisions and nothing above them. [verified] B15003, which the modern file also carries, splits the grades below ninth more finely and has no 2009 counterpart. It was read and agrees with B15002 on every figure quoted here. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population by race (B02001) and Hispanic origin (B03003)
series.unit: residents identifying as Black or African American alone, Allen County

points.label: Allen County population by race, 2023
points.method: 2023 five-year estimates. Race categories are "alone" except the two-or-more column; Hispanic origin is asked separately and overlaps every race column, so the rows do not sum to 100. The twelve townships and Lima partition the county: 2,515 plus 8,290 is 10,805, the county row. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population enumerated as Negro, Allen County

points.label: Allen County population by race and nativity, 1920
points.method: Read from page images rendered at 300 dpi, because the text layer of both volumes garbles digits — it renders Lima's row as "4l, 320 40,0li2 OU. \l". Two arithmetic checks were run before any figure was written down: the county's race lines sum to the printed total, and the city's white lines sum to the printed total white. The county figure is the compendium's, which is the federal count; the city figure is the abstract's, which is the same census. Where the county history and the census disagree, both are given and neither quotation is altered. [verified]

points.label: Allen County population by race, 1930–1960
points.method: Read from page images rendered at 250 to 300 dpi, because three of the four volumes have no text layer and the fourth's is OCR that garbles every digit. Each census was taken from the table that prints race by sex, and each column was added before it was written down: the four or seven race lines sum to the printed county total in every year, the twelve townships sum to the county in 1940 and 1960, and the four county totals — 69,419, 73,303, 88,183 and 103,691 — match the figures this corpus already held from a different volume. The label is the census's own for each year and is not modernised. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population enumerated as Negro, Black, or Black or African American alone, Allen County

points.label: Allen County population by race, 1970–2020
points.method: 1970 and 1980 read from page images rendered at 300 dpi, because neither volume has a text layer; 1990, 2000 and 2010 from `pdftotext -layout` on volumes that extract exactly; 2020 computed from the pipe-delimited redistricting file. Each census was checked against something it did not have to agree with: 1970's race and sex rows both sum to its printed county total and its five named other races to their printed subtotal; the thirteen county subdivisions sum to the county in every printed column in 1980, 1990 and 2020; the 2000 and 2010 race categories sum to their printed county totals; and the 2020 file's own hierarchy closes at every level — six single races to the one-race line, fifteen pairs to the two-race line, the four multiple lines to the two-or-more line, and that to the total. The county totals 111,144, 112,241, 109,755, 108,473, 106,331 and 102,206 are the figures this corpus already held from unrelated products. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population in group quarters, Allen County

points.label: Allen County group quarters, 2020
points.method: Table P5, Group Quarters Population by Major Group Quarters Type, from the Ohio file of the 2020 Census Redistricting Data Summary File (P.L. 94-171). Summed from the 3,552 block records for county 39003, joined to the geographic header on LOGRECNO. The block sums close on the file's own county record exactly, in every one of the ten cells. [verified] The Census Bureau's API serves the same table from the Demographic and Housing Characteristics file and refuses the request without a key, which is why the flat file was taken instead — the same reason this corpus reads the ACS from its summary file rather than its API. Institution identification is by geometry, not by address: a block is identified with a landmark only where the two carry the same land area and the same internal point. Two do. [inference] — see [a block can be a fence](../../decisions/a-block-can-be-a-fence.yml). The 2020 census applied disclosure avoidance to every published figure in this table, at every geography. The sentence that stood here — that the county totals are not noisy — was wrong: the census holds three quantities invariant and a county's group-quarters population is not among them. What is invariant is the number and major type of each occupied group-quarters facility in each block, which is a different fact and is not published as a number. [verified] — the technical documentation of [the characteristics file](../../catalog/census-2020-dhc.md), chapter 4; see [the total is enumerated and the split is not](../../decisions/the-total-is-enumerated-and-the-split-is-not.yml). Nothing in this node is withdrawn: the two large correctional cells are corroborated by the geometry they sit on, and that corroboration is what carries them, not an invariance they never had.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population outside the civilian noninstitutionalized universe, Allen County

points.label: Allen County's institutional population, 2019–2023
points.method: Tables B01001 and B18101 from the 2019–2023 five-year American Community Survey summary file, differenced cell by cell. B18101's six age brackets by sex — under 5, 5 to 17, 18 to 34, 35 to 64, 65 to 74, 75 and over — are matched by summing B01001's twenty-three brackets per sex into the same six. The two tables' totals for each sex close on their own published totals. [verified] The difference is institutionalized civilians plus all active-duty military, since "civilian noninstitutionalized" excludes both. The military part is isolated by a second subtraction: B01001's population 18 and over less B21001's civilian population 18 and over, which is 64 in this county and 1,286,167 nationally. [verified] No one under 18 is in either force, and the 5-to-17 difference of 15 is small enough to be sampling noise in a five-year estimate. [inference] Universes are read from the table shells published with the file, which are the only place they appear; the data files carry no universe field. [verified] Rate margins are ratio-estimate margins at the 90 per cent level, computed as the Census Bureau directs. The bounds on the county-wide disability share are arithmetic, not statistical: they assume nothing about the excluded population beyond its size. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: population under 18

points.label: Allen County's children, 2010–2024
points.method: County age-sex estimate files `CC-EST2020-AGESEX-39.csv` and `cc-est2024-agesex-39.csv`, Allen County, columns `UNDER5_TOT`, `AGE513_TOT` and `AGE1417_TOT`, summed here for the under-18 figure, which the files do not publish directly. The `YEAR` column is a code, not a year: in the 2010s file 1 is the 2010 census, 2 the estimates base, 3 to 12 the July estimates for 2010 through 2019, 13 the 1 April 2020 estimate and 14 the 1 July 2020 estimate; in the 2020s file 1 is the 2020 base and 2 to 6 the July estimates for 2020 through 2024. [verified] — the Bureau's own file layout. Births are `BIRTHS{year}` from `co-est2019-alldata.csv` and `co-est2024-alldata.csv`. The two series are never differenced across 1 July 2020.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: post-secondary students enrolled, Allen County

points.label: Higher education in Allen County, 2023
points.method: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System, 2023-24 collection. Institutions selected by the directory file's `COUNTYCD` equal to 39003, which returns six, all of them active. Autumn headcount and full-time equivalent from the derived enrolment file; twelve-month unduplicated headcount from the twelve-month enrolment file at level 1, all students; awards from the completions file, first majors only, with the institution-total rows excluded; housing capacity and price from the institutional characteristics files. [verified] Award levels are the file's own eight categories rather than a simplification, because two of them — certificates under twelve weeks and certificates of twelve weeks to a year — are together 38 per cent of everything this county awards, and a table that collapses them into "certificates" hides the shape of what two of the six institutions do. [inference] Both totals close: the six institutions' awards sum to 2,918 by institution and by level, and to the same figure across the field families. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: presidential votes by township and ward, Allen County

points.label: Allen County presidential vote by township and ward, 1884
points.method: Read from a 600-dpi render of the archive.org scan, not from OCR. Both OCR passes available for this book — the djvu text and the PDF text layer — return the Republican figure for Lima's Third Ward as 108, and the page says 103; the typeface's 3 and 8 are near-identical at scanning resolution and the difference is exactly the five votes that reconcile the Republican column to its printed total. That reconciliation is the check on the whole column. The Democratic column has no such check and is one short. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: presidential votes cast

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 2016
points.method: Summed by candidate over the county's 88 precincts. The 2016 file carries no registered-voter or ballots-cast column, so no turnout rate is derivable from it. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 2020
points.method: Summed by candidate over the county's 88 precincts. The total is 360 fewer than the 48,353 ballots cast — an undervote of 0.7 per cent. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: presidential votes cast, Allen County

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1856–1884
points.method: Read from the archive.org scan of the 1885 volume at 320 to 600 dpi rather than from its OCR, because the typeface confuses 3 with 8 and the OCR inherits the confusion: it renders the Republican vote of Lima's Third Ward as 108 where the page says 103, and Greeley's county vote as 2,403 where the page says 2,463. Each year's presidential figures were checked against the same year's other offices on the same page, which in this county run within a few dozen votes of the head of the ticket. Totals in the table above are this corpus's addition of the candidate columns the book prints, not figures the book prints. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1888–1908
points.method: Every figure read from a page render; no figure taken from a text layer, which for these volumes is either column-major and unassemblable or row-major and wrong — it gives Allen 3,079 and 4,946 in 1892 where the page prints 3,579 and 4,945. Totals: 1892, 1900 and 1908 are the volumes' own printed total-vote columns and "others" is the residual; 1888, 1896 and 1904 are abstracts with every candidate column, and the total is this corpus's addition. 1888 and 1904 check against printed plurality columns, 1892 and 1896 and 1900 and 1908 against a second printing of the same county row in a different volume. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1920
points.method: Read from a 400-dpi render of the Google scan, which has no text layer at all. The row checks itself against the volume's own plurality column: the printed Republican plurality of 2,320 is exactly 13,978 less 11,658, so a misread digit in either of the two leading figures would break the identity. The total of 26,082 is this corpus's addition of the four candidate columns; the volume prints no county-row total. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1960 and 1964
points.method: Read from the archive.org OCR of the 1967 volume rather than from its 212 MB scan. The county table's last three columns lag one row in that OCR — Adams's triple prints under Allen's code, Allen's under Ashland's name — so every figure here was taken from Table 3, the metropolitan areas, where the Lima row is Allen County exactly and no lag occurs, and then checked back against the lagged position in Table 2. The 1960 population printed beside the vote in Table 3 is 103,691, which is the county's own census figure and is what identifies the row. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 1980–1996
points.method: `ELE.zip` from the 2011 compendium, unzipped to a single spreadsheet with **nine worksheets**; a converter that reads only the first returns ten of the eighty-four items and looks complete. The item codes carry the year less 1800, so 1980 is `180` and 2000 is `200`, which puts two elections of the same measure under prefixes that look like different measures. Candidate names are this corpus's, from the party column and the year; the file names no person. Ranks and majority counts were computed from the file's own vote counts rather than from its rounded percentages, because a county at 50.04 per cent prints as 50.0. [verified]

points.label: Allen County presidential vote, 2000–2016
points.method: The lab's public GitHub mirror was read rather than its Dataverse deposit, whose data file is behind a guestbook — a form for a person to fill in, not a request this corpus makes on its behalf. That mirror stops at 2016, which is why 2020 here is the figure already held from OpenElections and why 2024 is absent altogether. The OpenElections files are county-level for 2000 and 2012 and a combined general file for 2008; the 2012 arbiter is `2012/FinalResults.xlsx` in the same repository, read from its XML parts because no spreadsheet library is installed. Ohio's own site was probed again and refuses every client. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: private employment by industry sector, Allen County

points.label: Allen County employment by sector, 1986 and 2022
points.method: County Business Patterns county files for 1986 and 2022, with sector 62 traced across 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020. Both endpoint years close exactly: the ten 1986 SIC divisions sum to 45,917 and the twenty 2022 NAICS sectors to 42,814, each equal to its file's own total row. Government, the self-employed and farms are excluded. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: private establishments on the business register

points.label: Allen County's private employers, 1986–2023
points.method: County files for every year 1986 to 2023, fipstate 39 and fipscty 003, read case-insensitively because the column names are lower case through 2014 and upper case afterwards, and with the smallest size class taken from `n1_4` through 2016 and `n<5` from 2017. [verified] The total row is `sic` `----` through 1997 and `naics` `------` from 1998. Payroll is `ap`, annual payroll in thousands of dollars; payroll per employee divides it by `emp`, the March 12 headcount, and is therefore an average over full-time and part-time workers alike. Real figures use the annual average of `CUUR0000SA0` unless the Midwest series is named. The sector comparison begins in 1998 because the 1997/1998 join changes the classification from SIC to NAICS.

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: properties listed on the National Register of Historic Places

points.label: Allen County on the National Register, 1966–2004
points.method: Layers 0 and 1 of the NPS `nrhp_locations` map service queried on `State='OHIO' AND County='Allen'` and unioned — 26 points and 3 polygons, no property in both. Polygon centroids computed here from the returned rings. Each of the 29 resulting coordinates put to the Allen County GIS township and section layers. Certification dates are the file's two-digit years read as 19xx above 30 and 20xx below. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: proprietors as a share of all employment

points.label: Allen County proprietors and payroll employment, 1969–2022
points.method: BEA's county employment tables, Ohio files, GeoFIPS 39003. Line 10 is total employment, 20 wage and salary, 40 proprietors, 50 farm proprietors and 60 nonfarm proprietors; 40 is 50 plus 60 in every year checked. The two tables are separate series on separate classifications and the join at 2000–2001 moves total employment by 3,148 and proprietors by 742, so no rate of change here crosses it. Industry detail in these files is suppressed as `(D)` for small cells and none of it is read. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: public library income from all sources

points.label: Allen County's public libraries, 2024
points.method: The FY2024 public-use administrative-entity and outlet files, filtered to `STABR` OH and `CNTY` ALLEN. Three administrative entities and eight outlets. County totals are the sum of the three reported rows and are not adjusted for the two service areas that cross the county line, which is why they are reported as service-area figures and never as per-resident-of-Allen-County figures. State and national comparisons are computed over the same file. Every quoted cell carries an `R_24` reported flag. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: pupils chronically absent, Allen County

points.label: Chronic absenteeism in Allen County, 2013–2022
points.method: The Civil Rights Data Collection's chronic-absenteeism tables for 2013, 2015, 2017, 2020, 2021 and 2022, read through the Urban Institute's mirror, filtered to the sex total and summed over the race dimension excluding its own all-pupils code. [verified] Schools are identified by `ncessch`; the 2020 vintage publishes a blank district identifier and a query filtered on that field returns nothing for this county. [verified] Rates use this collection's enrolment for the same year and the same schools. For 2022 there is no such enrolment and no rate is computed. [verified] Chronic absenteeism is the collection's own definition — absent fifteen or more school days in the year, for any reason, excused or not — and is not the state's ten-per-cent definition. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: pupils enrolled in an Advanced Placement course

points.label: Who takes the advanced courses in Allen County, 2021
points.method: Rates use the collection's own enrolment rather than the district files', because a numerator from one collection over a denominator from another is wrong before anything is measured; the two differ by 1.9 per cent across these ten schools. [verified] The race dimension carries its own total at code 99, so the county figure is that row and not a sum over the race codes. [verified] Reserved codes are excluded from both numerator and denominator: a school whose AP enrolment reads `-2` has answered that it offers no such course, and neither its pupils nor its zero enter an AP rate. [verified] The standardisation applies each school's white rate to that school's Black enrolment and sums, which is a direct standardisation on the school and removes the difference in which buildings the two groups attend. [verified] Ohio comparisons run over every school in the state with a twelfth grade and a positive enrolment, on the same rules. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: pupils suspended out of school at least once, Allen County

points.label: School discipline in Allen County, 2011–2021
points.method: The Civil Rights Data Collection for 2011, 2013, 2015, 2017, 2020 and 2021, read through the Urban Institute's mirror of the federal files, filtered to the disability and sex totals and summed over the race dimension excluding its own all-pupils code. [verified] Schools are identified by `ncessch` and not by district, because the 2020 vintage publishes a blank district identifier on every row; and rows with a blank school identifier are dropped, because the 2011 vintage carries some and they hold 6,208 pupils that belong to no school. [verified] — see [a total is checked against one it did not come from](../../decisions/a-total-is-checked-against-one-it-did-not-come-from.yml). Out-of-school suspension is the sum of the single-suspension and multiple-suspension columns, which count pupils and are mutually exclusive. Rates use this collection's own enrolment and never the Common Core's, which is 0.6 to 8.0 per cent larger in the same years. [verified] The county is its twelve districts as the district directory reports them, including Apollo Career Center and two community schools, and including the Delphos City schools that stand in Van Wert County. [inference]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: railroad main track in the county

points.label: Allen County's railroads, 1872–1921
points.method: Read from the full text of three county histories on archive.org, the 1885 book in two independent scans. The mileage is the 1885 book's, compiled from official records of 1883 and prefaced "about". The employment figures are as the sources print them: a range for 1879, a floor for the shops in 1906, and an exact count for the yards and freight offices in 1905. Nothing here averages a range or treats "more than 500" as 500, and the three are not added together. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: recordable work-related injuries and illnesses, Form 300A summaries

points.label: Allen County workplace injuries and illnesses, 2016–2024
points.method: Ohio rows pulled from nine annual releases and assigned to counties by address: the Census batch geocoder first, then [the county's own address points](../../catalog/allen-county-gis-downloads.md) for what it could not match, then TIGERweb point-in-polygon on a coordinate for the residue. Rows reporting more hours per employee than a year contains — 13 of 1,597 — are dropped; see [an impossible value is not an outlier](../../decisions/an-impossible-value-is-not-an-outlier.yml). Fifteen rows in Lima, Elida and Delphos could not be placed and are excluded. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: recorded drinking water violations in Allen County

points.label: Drinking water violations in Allen County, 1984–2026
points.method: All rows for systems whose identifier begins `OH02`, whatever the system's type or current status — so a tavern that closed in 1998 is counted. Health-based is the file's own `is_health_based_ind`, not a threshold chosen here. Distinct problems are counted by grouping on system and return-to-compliance date, which merges Bluffton's ten quarterly rows and leaves every other health-based violation on its own. The 2020s figure covers six years and eight months, not ten. [verified]

series.subject: place/allen-county.yml
series.parameter: recorded oil and gas wells

points.label: Oil and gas wells in Allen County
points.method: Two ODNR services, paged 1,000 rows at a time. [verified] The map service gives 4,849 rows for `WL_CNTY='ALLEN'` and the feature service 4,834 for `API_NO LIKE '34003%'`; 4,831 are in both, 18 in the map only and 1 in the feature service only. Counts of wells use the map service and counts of statuses, dates and depths use the feature service, which is the register the map is drawn from; the two disagree about the status of 2,933 of the 4,831 they share, and [the legend is not the record](../../decisions/the-legend-is-not-the-record.yml) is why the register wins. series.subject: place/lima.yml
series.parameter: frost-free days between the last spring and first autumn minimum at or below 32 °F

points.label: Allen County frost-free season, 1902–2025
points.method: Computed from daily minimum temperatures at GHCN-Daily station USC00334551, converted from tenths of a degree Celsius. Values carrying a non-blank quality flag are discarded before the count — 323 minima in the record, almost all failing an internal consistency check. The season is the number of days strictly between the two freezes, so a last freeze on 25 April and a first on 24 October is 181 days. [verified] A single station measures a single yard. The claim this node makes about the county rests on the Van Wert station agreeing with it, and on the county's own divisional record moving the same way over the same century; it does not rest on the Lima thermometer alone. [inference]

series.subject: place/lima.yml
series.parameter: highest and lowest daily temperature recorded, Allen County
