Values carrying a non-blank quality flag are discarded — 276 maxima and 323 minima, chiefly on internal consistency. The extremes above are taken from every surviving observation; the threshold counts per year use only the years carrying at least 350 daily maxima, which is 113 of the 124 complete calendar years from 1902 to 2025. The eleven excluded are 1921 and ten scattered between 1980 and 2019, six of them in the 1980s, which is why that decade's row rests on 1983, 1984, 1986 and 1989. [verified] A single station is a single yard, and the county has no second long daily record inside it. Every threshold here is therefore a statement about the Lima station, and the claims about the county rest on the divisional record agreeing with it. [inference]

points.method: The elevation image service was exported over the cut at one metre in EPSG:26916 and the channel bottom traced row by row as the minimum within thirty metres of the previous row. The pound is the longest run of rows whose bottom lies within 0.25 metres of the median of the run; it ends 168 rows short of the raster's north edge and 188 short of its south, so it is bounded by the ground and not by the request. [verified] Depths are measured in each row's cross-section from the traced bottom: the crest is the highest cell within 100 metres either side, the fields are the median of the cells 150 to 250 metres out on each side, averaged. [verified] The volume is the area between the surface and a straight line joining the fields at a stated half-width, integrated over the pound, and is reported as the range it takes over half-widths of 80 to 170 metres. [inference] Every figure is in feet at 3.280839895 to the metre.

assertions.statement: The realignment of 1896 did not reach Allen County. citations.node_label: School buildings in Allen County's twelve districts, 1986–2024

citations.span: **The two vacancy rates the Bureau publishes leave the largest class out of both of them.** The homeowner rate is for-sale-only over owner-occupied plus for-sale plus sold-not-occupied; the rental rate is for-rent over renter-occupied plus for-rent plus rented-not-occupied. Seasonal units, migrant-worker units and other-vacant units appear on neither side of either line. [verified] — [the same appendix](../../catalog/census-2020-dhc.md), B-21.

citations.node_label: Why Allen County's housing was empty, 2010 and 2020
citations.span: **So 1,568 of the county's housing units — 3.5 per cent of the stock — are empty and invisible to every vacancy rate the census publishes.** [inference] — the Bureau's own three formulas, applied here to its own eight rows. Both rates fell over the decade and the residual fell faster, which is a fact about the county the rates do not carry.

caveats: **This corpus cannot say why any particular house in Allen County is empty.** The census asked an enumerator to classify a vacant unit and published seven reasons and a remainder; the remainder is the largest of the eight, and nothing in this file or any other this corpus holds distinguishes a house being renovated from a house nobody wants.

citations.node_label: Who owns Allen County's houses, 2010 and 2020
citations.span: The county's owner-occupancy rate is the one figure of this kind the corpus already had, from a survey. [verified] — [the housing stock](allen-county-housing-stock-2023.yml). Counted instead of estimated, and split three ways rather than two, it is a different story: **the county lost 1,342 households that own with a mortgage and gained 616 that own outright and 1,042 that rent.** [verified] — [the 2020 characteristics file](../../catalog/census-2020-dhc.md) and [the 2010 summary file](../../catalog/census-2010-sf1.md), table H4 in both.

citations.node_label: Who owns Allen County's houses, 2010 and 2020
citations.span: **The survey does not publish the middle two rows and they are where the decade happened.** Owner occupancy fell 2.3 points and the count of owners fell by 726, but the mortgaged fell by 1,342 — nearly twice as far — because 616 households moved the other way and finished paying. [inference] — the same two tables, differenced here. A count of owners is two populations that behave differently and this corpus had been reading them as one.

caveats: **This corpus cannot say how much of the county's thirty-six-point ownership gap is the city.** The gap survives inside Lima at twenty points and outside it at thirty, so it is not only an address; separating what remains would need income, age, length of residence and the order in which a household arrived at its tenure, and this file carries a householder's race and nothing else about them.

citations.span: **"In 1933 Lima changed its city government from the Manager-Commission form to Mayor-Council."** [verified] — [History of Lima, Ohio](../../catalog/hackman-history-of-lima-1951.md), the booklet's chronology of the 1930s.

caveats: **This corpus cannot say how the change was made.** A charter amendment, a repeal, a new charter and a vote of the electors are all consistent with a booklet that gives a year and names no instrument, no ballot and no majority.

assertions.statement: The seventeen years the commission charter node could say nothing about are now eleven and six, with a dated change between them: the charter took effect on 1 January 1922 and the office of mayor returned in 1933.

citations.node_label: Lima abolishes the mayor, January 1, 1922
citations.span: **The office returned in 1933, and the commission form lasted eleven years.** [verified] — [History of Lima, Ohio](../../catalog/hackman-history-of-lima-1951.md); see [the return](lima-returns-to-mayor-and-council-1933.yml). The mayor the corpus found cutting twelve men from the street department in November 1939 was serving under a form of government six years old, and the seventeen years this node could say nothing about are now eleven and six with a dated change between them.

assertions.statement: Motor buses began replacing Lima's electric street cars in 1938, cars that had served the city for over fifty years. It is the end of a street railway this site could follow under four company names from June 1878 to 1921 and no further.

citations.node_label: Motor buses begin replacing Lima's street cars, 1938
citations.span: **"It was in 1938 that motor busses began replacing the electric street cars that had served the city for over fifty years."** [verified] — [History of Lima, Ohio](../../catalog/hackman-history-of-lima-1951.md), the booklet's chronology of the 1930s.

caveats: **This corpus cannot say when the last electric car ran in Lima.** A process that began in 1938 may have taken a month or a decade, and nothing read here follows it.

assertions.statement: Two Lima histories a generation apart put the first electric car on the Fourth of July and differ by a year: the 1921 county history has 1886, and a booklet of 1952 has the street railway converted on July 4th, 1887.

citations.node_label: The first electric car in Lima, July 4, 1886
citations.span: **A second local historian puts it on the same day of a different year.** "In 1887 an electric generating plant was built and on July 4th, the street railway was converted to an electric line, among the first of its kind". [verified] — [History of Lima, Ohio](../../catalog/hackman-history-of-lima-1951.md). Two Lima histories a generation apart agree on the Fourth of July and differ by one year, and neither cites anything. The `occurred` date stays at 1886 because the earlier book is nearer the event, and the disagreement is recorded rather than resolved. [inference] See [three witnesses and three dates](../../decisions/three-witnesses-and-three-dates.yml).

assertions.statement: The Lima Locomotive Works was "now known as the Baldwin-Lima-Hamilton Corp." by 1951, and descends from Carnes, Harper & Co., organized in 1869 to make sawmill machinery. Both ends of the chronology are one sentence each and neither transition is dated.

citations.node_label: Lima Locomotive Works
citations.span: **The end of the name is dated to within a year and the beginning to within one company.** By 1951 the Lima Locomotive Works was "now known as the Baldwin-Lima-Hamilton Corp.", and the works descend from Carnes, Harper & Co., organized in 1869 for the manufacture of sawmill machinery. [verified] — [History of Lima, Ohio](../../catalog/hackman-history-of-lima-1951.md). That is a merger history in two words and an origin in one sentence, from a chamber of commerce booklet that names no date for either transition.

citations.node_label: Allen County's stream network, 2026
citations.span: **Two miles in three of it are dry part of the year: 468.57 miles are intermittent stream against 174.17 perennial, with 79.90 miles of artificial path and 9.82 of canal or ditch.** [verified] — the same source, by the `FCode` labels the service publishes on its own renderer.

caveats: **This file cannot say which of these channels somebody dug.** Allen County's ground is prime farmland because it was drained, and a drained county's watercourses are largely ditches; the network classes 9.82 miles as canal or ditch and 468.57 as intermittent stream, and offers no field that would separate a straightened creek from a cut one.

assertions.statement: Hog Creek and Little Hog Creek do not meet and then enter the Ottawa River. Both creeks' lowest reaches name the same reach as the one below them, and that reach is the river.

citations.node_label: Little Hog Creek
citations.span: **It is the same point, and that field is what says so.** Both creeks' lowest reaches carry the same `dnhydroseq`: the reach `04100007000241`, named Ottawa River, with 233.83 square kilometres of drainage above it. Hog Creek brings 174.63 of that and this creek 57.54, and both reaches end at 40.77099, −83.95570. [verified] — [USGS NHDPlus High Resolution](../../catalog/usgs-nhdplus-high-resolution.md). The two creeks do not meet and then enter the river. The river is where they meet.

citations.node_label: Hog Creek
citations.span: **The flow network confirms the confluence and adds which creek is the main stem.** This creek's lowest reach and Little Hog Creek's carry the same `dnhydroseq` — the reach `04100007000241`, named Ottawa River — and both end at 40.77099, −83.95570. This creek brings 174.63 square kilometres to that point and Little Hog Creek 57.54, and the Ottawa's first reach names this one as its upstream main path. [verified] — [USGS NHDPlus High Resolution](../../catalog/usgs-nhdplus-high-resolution.md).

caveats: GNIS is consistent with that and does not establish it: what the file shows is that the name attaches today to the upper tributary only.

assertions.statement: That the Auglaize River joins the Maumee at Defiance has been an inference in this corpus since genesis, because a names file cannot establish it. A flow network can.

citations.node_label: Auglaize River
citations.span: **It joins the Maumee, and the corpus no longer has to assume it.** The Auglaize's main stem is 188 reaches and 181.6 kilometres, ending on 6,359.42 square kilometres of drainage and an estimated 2,087 cubic feet a second; the reach below it is `04100009001411`, named Maumee River, with 14,119.40. [verified] — [USGS NHDPlus High Resolution](../../catalog/usgs-nhdplus-high-resolution.md). The `flows-into` edge below has been `[inference]` since genesis and the mouth property said "Joins the Maumee River. [inference]"; both are now read from the receiving reach. See [a level path is not a river](../../decisions/a-level-path-is-not-a-river.yml), which is the rule that stopped this being answered *Saint Joseph River*.

citations.node_label: Maumee River
citations.span: **The Auglaize does join this river at Defiance, and the flow network says so.** The Auglaize's last reach carries 6,359.42 square kilometres and the reach below it is `04100009001411`, named Maumee River, with 14,119.40. [verified] — [USGS NHDPlus High Resolution](../../catalog/usgs-nhdplus-high-resolution.md). The paragraph above says a names file cannot establish that. A flow network can, and `dnhydroseq` is the field.

assertions.statement: The main stem the Auglaize discharges into carries 323 reaches named Saint Joseph River and 300 named Maumee River, so reading the path instead of the reach would have moved Allen County's water to Indiana.

citations.node_label: Maumee River
citations.span: **The main stem this river lies on is mostly named for another river.** Of its 1,008 reaches, 323 are named Saint Joseph River and 300 Maumee River, because the network traces the larger tributary upstream at every fork. [verified] — the same source. Reading that ranking instead of the receiving reach would have had Allen County's water joining a river in Indiana; see [a level path is not a river](../../decisions/a-level-path-is-not-a-river.yml).

assertions.statement: Three nodes of this corpus said in so many words which field would settle them, and the field settled all three: Sugar Creek flows into the Ottawa, so does the Little Ottawa River, and Little Hog Creek meets Hog Creek at the same point rather than above it.

citations.node_label: Sugar Creek
citations.span: **It flows into the Ottawa River.** Its main stem is 61 reaches ending on 164.69 square kilometres of drainage and an estimated 53.4 cubic feet a second; the reach below it is `04100007000216`, named Ottawa River, with 784.91. [verified] — [USGS NHDPlus High Resolution](../../catalog/usgs-nhdplus-high-resolution.md). So the creek that may or may not have named a township joins the river the county seat stands on, downstream of the county and inside Putnam. [inference]

citations.node_label: Little Ottawa River
citations.span: **It flows into the Ottawa River, and it joins between the county's two gauges.** Its lowest reach ends at 40.70595, −84.15394 — thirty-nine metres from the mouth GNIS gives — carrying 42.51 square kilometres of drainage, and the reach below it is `04100007001465`, named Ottawa River, with 395.40. assertions.statement: Against the 22,433.9 acres of swamp forest mapped in Allen County at settlement, 973 acres of woody wetland survive and 1,731 acres of wetland of any kind — 4.3 per cent and 7.7 per cent.

citations.node_label: What grew in Allen County before the surveys, mapped
citations.span: **What is left of it, measured on the same ground by a satellite.** The National Land Cover Database puts 973 acres of woody wetland in this county in 2021 and 758 of emergent herbaceous wetland, 1,731 acres in all. Against the 22,433.9 acres of swamp forest this node maps, the wooded part that survives is 4.3 per cent and the whole wetland class is 7.7 per cent. [verified] — [the land cover database](../../catalog/mrlc-nlcd-land-cover.md); see [the series](allen-county-land-cover-2001-2021.yml). Neither figure is the same quantity as the other — one is a nineteenth-century vegetation reconstruction and the other a thirty-metre classification of what grows now — and the order of magnitude between them is the answer to how completely the swamp was drained. citations.span: **The one thing the file rules out is that the pupils left.** The county's high-school roll fell by 81 of 4,917 between 2013 and 2021, 1.6 per cent, against an Advanced Placement enrolment that fell by 51.1 per cent and a Black Advanced Placement enrolment that fell by 89.7. caveats: **This corpus does not infer that any district decided against the courses.** A programme can end because nobody renewed it.
